relevant_body_uses.text: [L1] A linear Lorentz map is a linear $L:V\to V$ with $\eta(Lv,Lw)=\eta(v,w)$ for all $v,w$; it is proper when $\det L=+1$ and orthochronous when $L(C^+)=C^+$ ([[def-lorentz-map-and-lorentz-group]]).

[L2] A spatial rotation of the frame is a linear $R:V\to V$ with $R(e_0)=e_0$, $R(S)\subseteq S$, $\delta(Rw,Rz)=\delta(w,z)$ on the spatial three-space $S$, and $\det(R|_S)=+1$ in $(e_1,e_2,e_3)$ ([[def-spatial-rotation-of-an-inertial-frame]]).
[L3] The extension $\widehat R=\operatorname{diag}(1,R)$ of a spatial rotation $R$ is a proper orthochronous Lorentz map ([[lem-boost-rotation-factorization]]).

[L4] For every $|\boldsymbol\beta|<1$ the passive boost satisfies $B(\boldsymbol\beta)e_0=\gamma(e_0-\beta_1e_1-\beta_2e_2-\beta_3e_3)$ and $B(\mathbf 0)=\operatorname{id}_V$; the map $\boldsymbol\beta\mapsto B(\boldsymbol\beta)e_0$ is injective ([[lem-boost-is-proper-orthochronous-with-inverse]]).

4.1 Consequently the set of passive boosts is a proper subset of $SO^+(V,\eta)$: the strict inclusion is witnessed by $\widehat R$. The factorization theorem $L=B(-\boldsymbol\beta)\widehat R_\beta$ of [[lem-boost-rotation-factorization]] therefore cannot drop its rotation factor in general: for $L=\widehat R$ the theorem produces the factorization $\widehat R=B(\mathbf 0)\widehat R$ with rotation factor $\widehat R|_S\neq\operatorname{id}_S$, and by clause (v) of that theorem $L$ is a passive boost if and only if that factor is the identity. [L3, step 2.1, algebra] ∎

**False claim:** every smooth Born-rigid future unit timelike field $n$ ([[def-sr-observer-congruence-and-kinematics]], [[def-sr-chart-tetrad-and-congruence-distinction]]) is locally a positive multiple of a Killing field: there is a positive smooth function $f$ on a neighbourhood of every point with $\mathcal L_{fn}\eta=0$ ([[thm-sr-smooth-local-herglotz-noether]]).

**Given:** The affine Minkowski space with an inertial chart $(x^0,x^1,x^2,x^3)$ in which $\eta=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$ and the flat covariant derivative differentiates components ([[def-sr-affine-minkowski-model]], [[def-inertial-frame-and-inertial-chart]], [[def-flat-covariant-derivative-on-affine-minkowski-space]]), the kinematics of a congruence with acceleration $a$, expansion $\theta$ and vorticity $\omega$ ([[def-sr-observer-congruence-and-kinematics]]), a length scale $L_0>0$, and the functions and curves of the Construction below.

[L1] Killing equation ([[thm-sr-smooth-local-herglotz-noether]], [F10] and steps 9.1, 10.1 there): for a smooth future unit timelike field $n$ with expansion $\theta$, acceleration one-form $a^\flat$ and the Lie derivative of the metric, $\mathcal L_n\eta=2\theta-\bigl(n^\flat\otimes a^\flat+a^\flat\otimes n^\flat\bigr)$; and for a positive smooth $f$, $\mathcal L_{fn}\eta=f\mathcal L_n\eta+df\otimes n^\flat+n^\flat\otimes df$, so $\mathcal L_{fn}\eta=0$ if and only if $\nabla_a(fn)_b+\nabla_b(fn)_a=0$.

6.1 Conclusion and clarifications: steps 1.1-5.1 construct a smooth future unit timelike field $n$ on the open set $W$ that is Born rigid ($\theta=0$) and irrotational ($\omega=0$), and step 5.1 shows that for every positive smooth $f$ the field $fn$ fails the Killing equation on every nonempty open subset; hence the claim of the Statement refuted section is false. The Rindler congruence is not a counterexample of this kind: its metric $-\rho^2d\theta^2+d\rho^2+dy^2+dz^2$ is independent of $\theta$, so $\partial_\theta$ is a Killing field and the unit field $\rho^{-1}\partial_\theta$ is a positive multiple of it ([[thm-sr-fermi-walker-and-rigid-observer-examples]] clause (b)). The rotational classification of [[thm-sr-smooth-local-herglotz-noether]] is untouched, because the present congruence is irrotational: the counterexample concerns the irrotational branch of Born-rigid motions. [step 5.1] ∎

A declared one-point data record of the vocabulary with positive declared uncertainty determines the parameter of an operational model uniquely: if a record $R$ of clause (c) of [[def-sr-experiment-interface-vocabulary]] is consistent with two parameters $\beta_1,\beta_2$ of one operational model $M$, then $\beta_1=\beta_2$.

[F1] The experimental-interface vocabulary: an operational model is a tuple $M=(S,\Theta,\theta,D,F)$ with $S$ nonempty, $\Theta\subseteq\mathbb R^m$ nonempty, $\theta:S\to\Theta$ surjective, $D$ assigning run descriptions and $F:\Theta\to\mathbb R^d$ a prediction map whose components are required, by the declared interpretation $(*)$, to be numbers the framework assigns to $D(s)$ with every intermediate quantity, frame, event, sign and unit declared; a data record $R=(N,z,\varepsilon,a)$ declares that each value lies in the closed box $\prod_j[z_{k,j}-\varepsilon_{k,j},z_{k,j}+\varepsilon_{k,j}]$ in the declared units; and clause (f) makes a consistency or comparison claim between a record and a model a separate claim requiring an explicitly declared comparison rule ([[def-sr-experiment-interface-vocabulary]]).

[F2] Doppler theorem clauses (i) and (ii): for inertial charts whose transition is $x'=B(\beta)x+b$ with $\beta\in\mathbb R^3$, $|\beta|<1$, the same future null wave covector $k$ with frame-$x$ data $(\omega,s)$ has frame-$x'$ data $(\omega',s')$ with $\omega'=\gamma(1-\beta\cdot s)\omega$, where $\gamma=(1-|\beta|^2)^{-1/2}$; and the rest observers of $x$ and $x'$, of four-velocities $c e_0$ and $c e'_0$, read the angular frequencies $\omega=-c k(e_0)$ and $\omega'=-c k(e'_0)$ ([[pthm-sr-null-wave-doppler-and-aberration]]).

[F3] Observer angular frequency and wave data: the observer of four-velocity $U_o=c n$, with $\eta(n,n)=-1$ and $n$ future, reads $\omega_n:=-c k(n)=-k(U_o)$ in the SI convention $x^0=ct$; a future null wave covector has frame components $k_a=(-\omega/c,(\omega/c)s_1,(\omega/c)s_2,(\omega/c)s_3)$ with $\omega>0$ and $|s|=1$ ([[def-sr-null-wave-covector-and-observer-frequency]]).

[F4] Frame-data lemma clauses (a),(b),(e): for a future null wave covector in a frame, $\varpi:=-k(e_0)>0$ and $|s|=1$; conversely, a covector whose frame components are $(-\varpi,\varpi s_1,\varpi s_2,\varpi s_3)$ with $\varpi>0$ and $|s|=1$ is a future null wave covector ([[lem-sr-null-covector-frame-data]]).

[F5] Passive boost: for $\beta$ with $|\beta|<1$ the map $B(\beta)$ is defined in an inertial frame's coordinates by $x'^0=\gamma(x^0-\beta\cdot x)$ and $x'=x+((\gamma-1)/|\beta|^2)(\beta\cdot x)\beta-\gamma\beta x^0$ for $\beta\neq0$, with $B(0)$ the identity, so that in the axis case $\beta=\beta e_1$ one has $x'^0=\gamma(x^0-\beta x^1)$, $x'^1=\gamma(x^1-\beta x^0)$ ([[def-lorentz-boost]]); it is a proper orthochronous Lorentz map, $B(\beta)^{-1}=B(-\beta)$, and $B(\beta)e_0=\gamma(e_0-\beta_1 e_1-\beta_2 e_2-\beta_3 e_3)$ ([[lem-boost-is-proper-orthochronous-with-inverse]]).

[F6] Inertial frame and chart: an inertial frame $(o;e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3)$ consists of an event $o\in A$ and an ordered basis of $V$ that is $\eta$-orthonormal, future and positively oriented; its chart is $x(p)=E^{-1}(p-o)$ with $E(u)=\sum_a u^a e_a$ ([[def-inertial-frame-and-inertial-chart]]).

[A1] Adopted ideal plane-wave model: an ideal monochromatic light wave in vacuum is modeled in any inertial chart by a dimensionless affine phase with future null wave covector, and an ideal observer of four-velocity $U_o=c n$ receiving this wave reads the frequency $\omega_n=-c k(n)$ ([[post-sr-ideal-plane-wave-model]]).

[F7] SI conventions: in every inertial chart $x^0=ct$ with $c>0$ in metres per second, spatial coordinates in metres, and the matrix of $\eta$ equal to $\mathrm{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$ ([[def-sr-si-units-and-coordinate-conventions]]).

Under an inertial transition $x'=\Lambda x+a$ with $\Lambda$ a proper orthochronous Lorentz matrix ([[def-inertial-frame-and-inertial-chart]]), the components of the same tensor transform by the rank-two law $T'^{ab}=\Lambda^a{}_c\Lambda^b{}_dT^{cd}$ ([[thm-sr-tensor-and-current-transformation]]\,(iii)); writing $F'(x'):=F(\Lambda^{-1}(x'-a))$ for the scalar, one gets $T'^{ab}=F'\Lambda^a{}_c\Lambda^b{}_d\eta^{cd}=F'\eta^{ab}$, because $\Lambda\eta^{-1}\Lambda^{\mathsf T}=\eta^{-1}$ for a Lorentz matrix. So the expression $F\eta^{-1}$ is manifestly covariant; yet by step 2.1 its local conservation is equivalent to constancy of the scalar $F$, which covariance does not require. [step 2.1]

**False claim:** the simultaneity relation $\eta(n,q-p)=0$ between events of the affine model is independent of the future unit timelike vector $n$ ([[def-sr-simultaneity-slice-and-rest-distance]]).

**Counterexample.** In an inertial chart let $p:=x^{-1}(0,0,0,0)$ and $q:=x^{-1}(0,1,0,0)$, so that $d:=q-p$ is spacelike with $\eta(d,d)=1$, and let $n:=e_0=(1,0,0,0)$ and $n':=\gamma\bigl(e_0+\tfrac35e_1\bigr)=\tfrac54(1,\tfrac35,0,0)$, a boost of speed $3c/5$ along the first axis. Then $\eta(n',n')=\tfrac{25}{16}\bigl(-1+\tfrac{9}{25}\bigr)=-1$, so $n'$ is also a future unit timelike vector; $\eta(n,d)=0$, so $p$ and $q$ are simultaneous relative to $n$ and lie in the slice $H(p,n)$; and $\eta(n',d)=\tfrac54\cdot\tfrac35=\tfrac34\ne0$, so $p$ and $q$ are not simultaneous relative to $n'$ and lie in different slices for $n'$. The two slices $H(p,n)$ and $H(p,n')$ are distinct three-dimensional affine hyperplanes through $p$. Hence simultaneity in the sense of [[def-sr-simultaneity-slice-and-rest-distance]] depends on the observer vector and is not an observer-independent relation.

Work in the oriented time-oriented affine Minkowski space $(A,V,\eta,C^+)$ ([[def-sr-affine-minkowski-model]]) with its inertial atlas ([[lem-affine-minkowski-charts-form-a-smooth-atlas]]) and the canonical identification of tangent spaces with $V$ ([[lem-tangent-space-of-affine-minkowski-space-is-v]]). The objects defined below are, in general, different objects, and the distinctions between them are part of the definition.

**(a) Chart and inertial chart.** A **chart** of the model is a diffeomorphism $u:U\to u(U)$ from a nonempty open subset $U\subseteq A$ onto an open subset of $\mathbb R^4$ ([[def-diffeomorphism-and-local-diffeomorphism-of-manifolds]], [[def-smooth-manifold]]), written with components $(u^0,u^1,u^2,u^3)$. An **inertial chart** is the global chart $x(p)=E^{-1}(p-o)$ of an inertial frame $(o;e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3)$ ([[def-inertial-frame-and-inertial-chart]]). A general chart need not be inertial: if $x$ is an inertial chart and $N:x(U)\to\mathbb R^4$ is a diffeomorphism onto its image which is not the restriction of an affine map, then $u:=N\circ x$ is a chart that is not inertial, because if $u$ were the inertial chart of a frame then $x\circ u^{-1}=N^{-1}$ would be affine by [[lem-inertial-chart-transitions-are-affine-lorentz]] and hence $N=(N^{-1})^{-1}$ would be affine as the inverse of an affine bijection, a contradiction; the map $N(y)=(y^0,y^1+(y^0)^2,y^2,y^3)$ on $\mathbb R^4$ is an explicit example.

**(b) Tetrad at an event and tetrad field.** A **tetrad at $p\in A$** is an ordered basis $(e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3)$ of $V$ with $\eta(e_a,e_b)=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)_{ab}$ and $e_0$ future, $e_0\in C^+$ ([[def-causal-classification-of-lorentz-vectors]], [[def-time-orientation-and-future-causal-sets]]): this is the basis of an inertial frame without an origin and without the orientation condition. A **tetrad field** on a nonempty open subset $\Omega\subseteq A$ is a tuple $(E_0,E_1,E_2,E_3)$ of smooth vector fields on $\Omega$ ([[def-ck-tensor-field-on-minkowski-space]], type $(1,0)$) whose values at every $p\in\Omega$ form a tetrad at $p$. A tetrad field is **observer-adapted** to a prescribed future timelike worldline or congruence when $E_0=U/c$ for the corresponding future timelike unit vector field $U$ with $\eta(U,U)=-c^2$ ([[def-sr-regular-causal-curve-and-worldline]]).

**(c) Observer congruence.** An **observer congruence** on a nonempty open subset $\Omega\subseteq A$ is a smooth vector field $n:\Omega\to V$ with $\eta(n,n)=-1$ and $n(p)\in C^+$ for every $p\in\Omega$. Its **observers** are its maximal integral curves ([[def-integral-curve-of-a-vector-field]], [[thm-unique-maximal-integral-curve-through-each-point]]). Each observer is a future timelike worldline ([[def-sr-regular-causal-curve-and-worldline]]): its tangent at a parameter value $s$ is $n(x(s))$, which is future timelike, and it is regular because $\eta(n,n)=-1$ makes $n$ nowhere zero. **Completeness** of the integral curves, a global product structure of $\Omega$, and global synchronization are not asserted by this definition.

- **Non-inertial charts exist, and the example is checked.** The map $N(y)=(y^0,y^1+(y^0)^2,y^2,y^3)$ is a diffeomorphism of $\mathbb R^4$ with the smooth two-sided inverse $z\mapsto(z^0,z^1-(z^0)^2,z^2,z^3)$. It is not the restriction of an affine map: $N(0)=0$ and $N(2e_0)=(2,4,0,0)\ne2N(e_0)=(2,2,0,0)$ for $e_0=(1,0,0,0)$, so $N$ is not linear, and with $N(0)=0$ it is therefore not affine. If $N\circ x$ were an inertial chart, the transition $x\circ(N\circ x)^{-1}=N^{-1}$ between inertial charts would be affine by [[lem-inertial-chart-transitions-are-affine-lorentz]]; the inverse of an affine bijection $z\mapsto Az+b$ of $\mathbb R^4$ is again affine, $w\mapsto A^{-1}w-A^{-1}b$ ([[def-lorentz-map-and-lorentz-group]]), so $N$ would be affine, a contradiction. Hence $N\circ x$ is a chart that is not inertial, and being $C^\infty$ it belongs to the model's smooth structure.

- **Tetrads exist at every event, and tetrad fields are smooth by components.** [[lem-lorentz-form-has-orthonormal-basis]] supplies an $\eta$-orthonormal basis $(f_0,f_1,f_2,f_3)$ of $V$; since $\eta(f_0,f_0)=-1<0$ the vector $f_0$ is timelike, so exactly one of $f_0$ and $-f_0$ lies in $C^+$ because the timelike set is the disjoint union of the two future and past cones ([[def-time-orientation-and-future-causal-sets]], [[def-causal-classification-of-lorentz-vectors]]), and negating it preserves $\eta$-orthonormality; no orientation condition is imposed on a tetrad, so this already produces a tetrad at any prescribed event. The formulation with the additional positive-orientation condition, and with an arbitrary origin, is the inertial-frame existence statement of [[lem-future-oriented-inertial-frames-exist]]. A tetrad field is componentwise smooth in an inertial chart by the definition of $C^k$ tensor fields on the affine model ([[def-ck-tensor-field-on-minkowski-space]], [[lem-tangent-space-of-affine-minkowski-space-is-v]]).

- **Congruences have well-defined observers.** A smooth unit field $n$ on $\Omega$ is a smooth map $\Omega\to V$ with values in the future timelike cone, and [[thm-unique-maximal-integral-curve-through-each-point]] supplies through every point a unique maximal integral curve of $n$ ([[def-integral-curve-of-a-vector-field]]); along such a curve the identity $\eta(n,n)=-1$ gives $\eta(x',x')=-1$ at every parameter value, so each observer is a future timelike worldline with future unit tangent, in particular regular ([[def-sr-regular-causal-curve-and-worldline]]). Nothing about completeness of the maximal domains is asserted.

**(a) Run descriptions.** A *run description* is a finite tuple $D=(d_1,\dots,d_r)$ whose entries are framework objects of the following kinds, each declared with its domain and regularity as specified by the cited item, together with the frame, observer, event or unit convention required for a numerical reading where such a reading is used: a point of the affine Minkowski space $A$ (an event, [[def-sr-affine-minkowski-model]]); a vector of $V$ of declared causal character ([[def-causal-classification-of-lorentz-vectors]]); a future timelike worldline together with its proper-time function ([[def-sr-regular-causal-curve-and-worldline]], [[def-sr-proper-time]]); a future unit timelike vector or a smooth observer congruence ([[def-sr-chart-tetrad-and-congruence-distinction]]); a future null wave covector with its affine phase ([[def-sr-affine-phase-and-wave-covector]]); a radar time or radar distance assigned by the operational radar protocol ([[def-sr-operational-radar-protocol]]); an observer angular frequency ([[def-sr-null-wave-covector-and-observer-frequency]]); an observer energy, spatial momentum, kinetic energy or invariant mass ([[def-sr-observed-energy-momentum-and-kinetic-energy]]); and a real parameter vector in a declared subset of $\mathbb R^m$ with declared units. A run description is a description of a model configuration; the tuple asserts nothing about any apparatus or about nature.

Let $(A,V,\eta,C^+)$ be the oriented time-oriented affine Minkowski model and let $c>0$ be a fixed mathematical speed scale, with the coordinate convention $x^0=ct$, let $(o;e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3)$ be an inertial frame with inertial chart $x$ and spatial Euclidean structure $(S,\delta,|\cdot|)$ ([[def-inertial-frame-and-inertial-chart]], [[def-spatial-euclidean-structure-of-an-inertial-frame]]), and write the points of $\mathbb R\times S$ as $(t,x)$.

(a) *Lorentz boost charts with a variable speed scale.* For $v\in S$ and a real $C>|v|$ put $\gamma_C(v):=(1-|v|^2/C^2)^{-1/2}$ ([[def-rational-power]]) and define the affine map $\Phi_{v,C}:\mathbb R\times S\to\mathbb R\times S$ by $$\Phi_{v,C}(t,x):=\Bigl(\gamma_C(v)\bigl(t-\tfrac{\delta(v,x)}{C^2}\bigr),\ \ x+\tfrac{\gamma_C(v)-1}{|v|^2}\delta(v,x)\,v-\gamma_C(v)\,t\,v\Bigr)\quad(v\ne0),$$ with $\Phi_{0,C}:=\mathrm{id}$; when $|v|<c$, at $C=c$ this is the coordinate expression, in the convention $x^0=ct$, of the passive Lorentz boost $B(v/c)$ of [[def-lorentz-boost]]: if an event has coordinates $(ct,x)$ in the unprimed inertial chart of the frame, then $\Phi_{v,c}(t,x)$ are its coordinates $(x'^0/c,\,x'^1,x'^2,x'^3)$ in the boosted inertial chart with parameter $v/c$.

(d) *Scope of the family.* The parameter $C$ is a variable speed scale inside a family of coordinate expressions; it is not a change of the model's adopted constant $c$, and the members with $C\ne c$ are auxiliary mathematical maps used only to state the limit of [[lem-sr-uniform-galilean-limit-of-boost-charts]]. Nothing here asserts a physical limit of the framework, and no limiting trajectory, force or interaction is defined.

- **Well-definedness.** For $v\ne0$ and $C>|v|$ the base $1-|v|^2/C^2$ lies in $(0,1]$; it equals $1$ only at $v=0$, which the nonvanishing branch excludes, so $\gamma_C(v)$ is a positive rational power ([[def-rational-power]]) and the displayed formulas assign to each pair $(t,x)\in\mathbb R\times S$ a pair of elements of $\mathbb R\times S$, using the bilinear form $\delta$ and the vector-space operations of $S$. For $v=0$ the coefficient $(\gamma_C(0)-1)/|0|^2$ in the nonvanishing branch is the indeterminate form $0/0$, so the map is declared separately to be the identity; this is the same convention as in [[def-lorentz-boost]]. The family is total in the parameter: for every $v$ the admissible speeds are exactly $C>|v|$, an open interval, and $C=c$ belongs to it precisely when $|v|<c$.

- **The identification at $C=c$ is a substitution.** Writing $\beta:=v/c$ and $x^0:=ct$ in the definition of $B(\beta)$ in [[def-lorentz-boost]] gives $x'^0=\gamma(x^0-\beta\cdot x)$ and $x'=x+\tfrac{\gamma-1}{|\beta|^2}(\beta\cdot x)\beta-\gamma\beta x^0$ with $\gamma=\gamma_c(v)$; since $\beta\cdot x=\delta(v,x)/c$, $|\beta|^2=|v|^2/c^2$ and $\beta x^0=(v/c)(ct)=vt$, this is exactly $x'^0/c=\gamma_c(v)(t-\delta(v,x)/c^2)$ and $x'=x+\tfrac{\gamma_c(v)-1}{|v|^2}\delta(v,x)v-\gamma_c(v)tv$, that is $\Phi_{v,c}$. The boost $B(v/c)$ is a linear map of $V$ acting on coordinates in the frame basis, while $\Phi_{v,c}$ is the induced affine coordinate expression on the chart domain $\mathbb R\times S$; those two descriptions agree by the displayed computation, which is why the definition records the identification rather than asserting a new map.

- **No uniform limit and no physical interpretation are asserted here.** The definition proves no limit of the family and states no convergence of trajectories; the bounded-region rate and the failure off bounded regions are proved in [[lem-sr-uniform-galilean-limit-of-boost-charts]]. The variable $C$ is an auxiliary parameter of a mathematical family, not a change of the model's adopted constant $c$; the model's Lorentz form, time orientation and inertial frames are those of [[def-sr-affine-minkowski-model]], and no choice principle is used.

(a) A **stress-energy tensor** on $\Omega$ of class $C^k$, $k\ge0$ (with $C^0$ meaning continuous), is a $C^k$ symmetric type-$(2,0)$ tensor field $T$ on $\Omega$ in the sense of [[def-ck-tensor-field-on-minkowski-space]]: at every $p\in\Omega$ the map $T(p):V^*\times V^*\to\mathbb R$ is bilinear and symmetric, so in every inertial chart its components satisfy $T^{ab}=T^{ba}$ ([[thm-sr-tensor-and-current-transformation]]\,(iii)).

(b) In each inertial chart $x$ of the model ([[def-inertial-frame-and-inertial-chart]]) define the component families $\varepsilon_x:=T^{00}$, $\pi_x^i:=T^{0i}/c=T^{i0}/c$ and $S_x^{ij}:=T^{ij}$. These are numerical component and scaling conventions involving the fixed positive number $c$; their transformation behaviour is inherited from $T$ and no physical units or measurement interpretation form part of this mathematical definition.

(c) When $k\ge1$, the **four-force density** of $T$ is the $C^{k-1}$ field whose inertial components are $f^b:=\partial_aT^{ab}$, where $\partial_a$ are the coordinate partial derivatives of [[def-directional-and-partial-derivatives]] and the sum over $a$ is the standard contraction of a contravariant index with a coordinate derivative. The components $\partial_aT^{ab}$ transform as a vector, so $f$ is a well-defined vector field on $\Omega$ independent of the inertial chart: under an inertial transition $x'=\Lambda x+a$ the components satisfy $\partial'_aT'^{ab}=\Lambda^b{}_d\,\partial_cT^{cd}$ ([[thm-sr-tensor-and-current-transformation]]\,(iv)), which is exactly the vector transformation law of clause (i) applied to the components $f^b$. For $k\ge1$ one says that $T$ is **locally conserved**, or **balanced**, on $\Omega$ when $f=0$ on $\Omega$, and that $T$ is **balanced against the four-force density** $f$ when $\partial_aT^{ab}=f^b$.

The symmetry condition in (a) is chart-independent by the rank-two component law ([[thm-sr-tensor-and-current-transformation]]\,(iii)): if $T^{ab}=T^{ba}$ in one inertial chart, then $T'^{ab}=\Lambda^a{}_c\Lambda^b{}_dT^{cd}=\Lambda^b{}_d\Lambda^a{}_cT^{dc}=T'^{ba}$ in every other. The constants $\varepsilon_x,\pi_x,S_x$ of (b) are numerical component conventions only; the physical readings of such components — energy density, momentum density, stress, force density — are model premises adopted separately in [[post-sr-matter-models-and-evolution]] and used in [[pthm-sr-local-stress-energy-conservation]]. Nothing in this definition requires the metric contraction $\eta_{ab}T^{ab}$ to have a sign, requires any energy condition, or asserts that a locally conserved field is the total stress-energy of an isolated system.

Hence the internal longitudinal material-metric length between labels $0$ and $L$ is $|e|_h L = \gamma(t) L > L$ for every $t \neq 0$, with minimum $L$ at $t = 0$, while the chart-frame separation is $q(t) + L - q(t) = L$ for every $t$ in $J$.

Its derivatives are $U:=x'=c(\cosh\theta,\sinh\theta,0,0)$ and $A:=U'=\alpha(\sinh\theta,\cosh\theta,0,0)$, and one computes $\eta(U,U)=c^2(-\cosh^2\theta+\sinh^2\theta)=-c^2$, $\eta(A,A)=\alpha^2(-\sinh^2\theta+\cosh^2\theta)=\alpha^2$ and $\eta(U,A)=c\alpha(-\cosh\theta\sinh\theta+\sinh\theta\cosh\theta)=0$; thus $\tau$ is a proper-time parameter (up to an additive constant) and $U$ is the four-velocity of a uniformly accelerated worldline. Put $X_0:=U/c=(\cosh\theta,\sinh\theta,0,0)$ and $X_1:=(\sinh\theta,\cosh\theta,0,0)$; then $\eta(X_0,X_0)=-1$, $\eta(X_0,X_1)=0$ and $\eta(X_1,X_1)=1$, so $(X_0,X_1)$ is an orthonormal pair. A direct substitution into the Fermi-Walker rule shows that both are Fermi-Walker transported: $X_0'=A/c$ equals $\frac1{c^2}\bigl(\eta(A,X_0)U-\eta(U,X_0)A\bigr)=\frac1{c^2}\bigl(0+cA\bigr)=A/c$, and $X_1'=\frac{\alpha}{c}X_0$ equals $\frac1{c^2}\bigl(\eta(A,X_1)U-\eta(U,X_1)A\bigr)=\frac1{c^2}\bigl(\alpha U-0\bigr)=\frac{\alpha}{c}X_0$. Moreover $X_1$ is not parallel transported, since $X_1'=\frac{\alpha}{c}X_0\ne0$ for $\alpha>0$; Fermi-Walker transport therefore differs from parallel transport for accelerated motion. The norm $\eta(X_1,X_1)=1$ is constant along the worldline, an instance of the preservation clause of [[thm-sr-fermi-walker-and-rigid-observer-examples]], and adjoining the constant fields $\partial_y,\partial_z$ gives a Fermi-Walker transported orthonormal tetrad $\bigl(U/c,X_1,\partial_y,\partial_z\bigr)$ along the hyperbolic worldline.

Explicit witness: the events $p:=x^{-1}(5,3,0,0)$ and $r:=x^{-1}(5,7,0,0)$ are simultaneous in $x$ (both have $x^0=5$) and separated by $4$; their $x'$-coordinates are $x'(p)=(4,0,0,0)$ and $x'(r)=(1,5,0,0)$, so they are not simultaneous in $x'$ but their $x'$-separation is $5=L_0$. Comparing events at equal $x'$-time instead: the events of the two worldlines with $x'^0=4$ are $x^{-1}(5,3,0,0)$ and $x^{-1}(35/4,37/4,0,0)$, the second of which has $x'^1=5$; at equal $x'$-time $4$ the endpoints are separated by $5$, the rest length. Thus the frame $x$ assigns length $4$ to a rod of rest length $5$ at rest in $x'$, exactly the contraction $L_0/\gamma$ of clause (ii) of [[lem-sr-boost-time-length-and-velocity-formulas]], and the comparison uses the simultaneity slice of the measuring frame in the sense of [[def-sr-simultaneity-slice-and-rest-distance]].

**Given:** Two inertial charts $x$, $x'$ of the affine Minkowski model related by the boost of speed $v=3c/5$ along the first axis with $\gamma=5/4$, the number $L_0=5$, the two worldlines $x'^1=0$ and $x'^1=5$ at rest in $x'$ with zero transverse coordinates, and the witness events $p=x^{-1}(5,3,0,0)$, $r=x^{-1}(5,7,0,0)$ ([[def-inertial-frame-and-inertial-chart]], [[def-sr-affine-minkowski-model]]).

[L1] The transition is $x'^0=\gamma\bigl(x^0-\tfrac35x^1\bigr)$, $x'^1=\gamma\bigl(x^1-\tfrac35x^0\bigr)$, $x'^2=x^2$, $x'^3=x^3$ with $\gamma=5/4$ ([[lem-sr-boost-time-length-and-velocity-formulas]], [[def-lorentz-boost]]).

[L2] Length comparison (clause (ii) of [[lem-sr-boost-time-length-and-velocity-formulas]]): two worldlines at rest in $x'$ with $x'$-separation $L_0$ have $x$-separation $L_0/\gamma$ at equal $x$-times, while at equal $x'$-times their $x'$-separation is $L_0$.

[L3] Simultaneity relative to a chart is equality of the chart's time coordinate, and the events simultaneous with $p$ in the frame $x$ are the slice $H(p,e_0)$ of the measuring frame ([[def-sr-simultaneity-slice-and-rest-distance]], [[def-inertial-frame-and-inertial-chart]]).

- **Which events are being compared.** The two witness events of step 1.2 are simultaneous in $x$ and not in $x'$, while the two events of step 1.3 are simultaneous in $x'$ and not in $x$; the contracted and the rest lengths therefore refer to different pairs of events on the same two worldlines, which is exactly the content of clause (ii) of [[lem-sr-boost-time-length-and-velocity-formulas]].

Then $M:=(S,\Theta,\theta,D,F)$ is an operational model for the dimensionless ratio $\omega_o/\omega$ in the sense of clause (b) of [[def-sr-experiment-interface-vocabulary]]: condition $(*)$ holds with the prediction supplied by the cited Doppler theorem, and $d=1$. The map $F$ is strictly decreasing on $(-1,1)$, and for every real $r>0$ there is exactly one $\beta\in(-1,1)$ with $F(\beta)=r$, namely

[F1] The experimental-interface vocabulary: an operational model is a tuple $M=(S,\Theta,\theta,D,F)$ with $S$ nonempty, $\Theta\subseteq\mathbb R^m$ nonempty, $\theta:S\to\Theta$ surjective, $D$ assigning run descriptions and $F:\Theta\to\mathbb R^d$ a prediction map whose components are required, by the declared interpretation $(*)$, to be numbers the framework assigns to $D(s)$ with every intermediate quantity, frame, event, sign and unit declared; a data record $R=(N,z,\varepsilon,a)$ declares that each value lies in the closed box $\prod_j[z_{k,j}-\varepsilon_{k,j},z_{k,j}+\varepsilon_{k,j}]$ in the declared units ([[def-sr-experiment-interface-vocabulary]]).

[F2] Doppler theorem clauses (i) and (ii): for inertial charts whose transition is $x'=B(\beta)x+b$ with $\beta\in\mathbb R^3$, $|\beta|<1$, the same future null wave covector $k$ with frame-$x$ data $(\omega,s)$ has frame-$x'$ data $(\omega',s')$ with $\omega'=\gamma(1-\beta\cdot s)\omega$, where $\gamma=(1-|\beta|^2)^{-1/2}$; and the rest observers of $x$ and $x'$, of four-velocities $c e_0$ and $c e'_0$, read the angular frequencies $\omega=-c k(e_0)$ and $\omega'=-c k(e'_0)$ ([[pthm-sr-null-wave-doppler-and-aberration]]).

[F3] Observer angular frequency and wave data: the observer of four-velocity $U_o=c n$, with $\eta(n,n)=-1$ and $n$ future, reads $\omega_n:=-c k(n)=-k(U_o)$ in the SI convention $x^0=ct$; a future null wave covector has frame components $k_a=(-\omega/c,(\omega/c)s_1,(\omega/c)s_2,(\omega/c)s_3)$ with $\omega>0$ and $|s|=1$ ([[def-sr-null-wave-covector-and-observer-frequency]]).

[F4] Frame-data lemma clauses (a),(b),(e): for a future null wave covector in a frame, $\varpi:=-k(e_0)>0$ and $|s|=1$; conversely, a covector whose frame components are $(-\varpi,\varpi s_1,\varpi s_2,\varpi s_3)$ with $\varpi>0$ and $|s|=1$ is a future null wave covector ([[lem-sr-null-covector-frame-data]]).

[F5] Passive boost: for $\beta$ with $|\beta|<1$ the map $B(\beta)$ is defined in an inertial frame's coordinates by $x'^0=\gamma(x^0-\beta\cdot x)$ and $x'=x+((\gamma-1)/|\beta|^2)(\beta\cdot x)\beta-\gamma\beta x^0$ for $\beta\neq0$, with $B(0)$ the identity, so that in the axis case $\beta=\beta e_1$ one has $x'^0=\gamma(x^0-\beta x^1)$, $x'^1=\gamma(x^1-\beta x^0)$ ([[def-lorentz-boost]]); it is a proper orthochronous Lorentz map, $B(\beta)^{-1}=B(-\beta)$, and $B(\beta)e_0=\gamma(e_0-\beta_1 e_1-\beta_2 e_2-\beta_3 e_3)$ ([[lem-boost-is-proper-orthochronous-with-inverse]]).

[F6] Inertial frame and chart: an inertial frame $(o;e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3)$ consists of an event $o\in A$ and an ordered basis of $V$ that is $\eta$-orthonormal, future and positively oriented; its chart is $x(p)=E^{-1}(p-o)$ with $E(u)=\sum_a u^a e_a$ ([[def-inertial-frame-and-inertial-chart]]).

[A1] Adopted ideal plane-wave model: an ideal monochromatic light wave in vacuum is modeled in any inertial chart by a dimensionless affine phase with future null wave covector, and an ideal observer of four-velocity $U_o=c n$ receiving this wave reads the frequency $\omega_n=-c k(n)$ ([[post-sr-ideal-plane-wave-model]]).

[F7] SI conventions: in every inertial chart $x^0=ct$ with $c>0$ in metres per second, spatial coordinates in metres, and the matrix of $\eta$ equal to $\mathrm{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$ ([[def-sr-si-units-and-coordinate-conventions]]).

[L1] Coordinate criterion and cone description: for a vector $v=(v^0,v_s)$ with spatial norm $|v_s|$, $v\in\overline{C^+}$ iff $v^0\ge|v_s|$, $v\in C^+$ iff $v^0>|v_s|$, and $v$ is future null exactly when $|v_s|=v^0>0$; for events $r,s$ with $D=x(s)-x(r)$, $s\in J^+(r)$ iff $D^0\ge|D_s|$ and $s\in I^+(r)$ iff $D^0>|D_s|$ ([[lem-sr-future-causal-sums-and-inertial-coordinate-criterion]]).

[L2] Causal classification: $\eta(v,v)=-(v^0)^2+|v_s|^2$ in the inertial basis; $v$ is null exactly when $v\ne 0$ and $\eta(v,v)=0$, and timelike when $\eta(v,v)<0$ ([[def-causal-classification-of-lorentz-vectors]]); the sum of two elements of $\overline{C^+}$ lies in $\overline{C^+}$, and if one of them lies in $C^+$ the sum lies in $C^+$ ([[lem-sr-future-causal-sums-and-inertial-coordinate-criterion]]).

[L3] Euclidean structure: for spatial coordinate vectors $p,q$ the norm satisfies $|p|^2=\sum_i(p^i)^2$, $|p|=0$ implies $p=0$, the triangle inequality $|p+q|\le|p|+|q|$ holds, and $|p+q|^2=|p|^2+2p\cdot q+|q|^2$ with the Euclidean scalar product $p\cdot q$ ([[def-euclidean-inner-product]], [[def-spatial-euclidean-structure-of-an-inertial-frame]], [[cor-triangle-inequality-for-inner-product-norm]]).
[L4] Chart linearity: coordinate differences of events are the coordinates of their displacement ([[def-inertial-frame-and-inertial-chart]]).

In an inertial chart $(x^0,x^1,x^2,x^3)$ of the affine Minkowski model with metric $\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$ let the observer be at rest at the spatial origin, so that its worldline is $x^1=x^2=x^3=0$, let $T>0$, and let $q:=x^{-1}\bigl(cT,\tfrac35cT,0,0\bigr)$, an event of chart time $T$ and spatial coordinate $(3cT/5,0,0)$. With $e_-:=x^{-1}\bigl(\tfrac25cT,0,0,0\bigr)$ and $e_+:=x^{-1}\bigl(\tfrac85cT,0,0,0\bigr)$ one has $q-e_-=\bigl(\tfrac35cT,\tfrac35cT,0,0\bigr)$ and $e_+-q=\bigl(\tfrac35cT,-\tfrac35cT,0,0\bigr)$; both displacements have $\eta$-square $-\tfrac{9}{25}c^2T^2+\tfrac{9}{25}c^2T^2=0$ and positive time component, hence are future null, so the radar protocol applies with emission $e_-$, reflection $q$ and reception $e_+$ ([[def-sr-operational-radar-protocol]], [[lem-sr-radar-midpoint-for-inertial-observer]]). Since the observer is inertial, its proper time between the chart times $\lambda_-=\tfrac25cT$ and $\lambda_+=\tfrac85cT$ is $(\lambda_+-\lambda_-)/c$ with the stated clock calibration, so the radar assignments are $\tau_{\mathrm{rad}}(q)=\tfrac12\bigl(\tfrac25T+\tfrac85T\bigr)=T$, the chart time of $q$, and $\rho_{\mathrm{rad}}(q)=\tfrac{c}{2}\bigl(\tfrac85T-\tfrac25T\bigr)=\tfrac35cT$, the chart distance of $q$ from the observer. Hence the two events $q$ and $q'$ of equal chart time are radar-simultaneous, with radar distances equal to their chart distances, in agreement with [[lem-sr-radar-midpoint-for-inertial-observer]].

For the two worldlines $y_a=y_0$ and $y_b=y_{L_0}$: (a) at the same $x'$-time $\lambda$ their $x'^1$-coordinates are $0$ and $L_0$, so the $x'$-separation is $L_0$. (b) At equal $x$-time $x^0=\tau$: for $y_a$ one has $\gamma(\lambda_a+0)=\tau$, hence $\lambda_a=\tau/\gamma$ and $x^1_a=\gamma(0+\beta\lambda_a)=\beta\tau$; for $y_b$ one has $\gamma(\lambda_b+\beta L_0)=\tau$, hence $\lambda_b=\tau/\gamma-\beta L_0$ and $x^1_b=\gamma\bigl(L_0+\beta(\tau/\gamma-\beta L_0)\bigr)=\gamma L_0(1-\beta^2)+\beta\tau=L_0/\gamma+\beta\tau$, using $\gamma(1-\beta^2)=1/\gamma$; therefore $x^1_b-x^1_a=L_0/\gamma$ for every $\tau$, which is the stated length assigned by the frame $x$ to the rod of rest length $L_0$ at rest in $x'$. (c) Exchanging the roles of the two frames replaces $\beta$ by $-\beta$ in the same computation (the inverse transition of step 1.1 has parameter $-\beta$), so two worldlines at rest in $x$ with $x$-separation $L_0$ have $x'$-separation $L_0/\gamma$ at equal $x'$-times; also (a) and (b) refer to different pairs of events unless $\beta L_0=0$, as demanded by the statement. [F3, step 1.1]

Let $(A,V,\eta,C^+)$ be an oriented time-oriented affine Minkowski space ([[def-sr-affine-minkowski-model]]), let $U\subseteq A$ be a nonempty open subset which, with the topology of [[lem-affine-minkowski-charts-form-a-smooth-atlas]], is path-connected and simply connected ([[def-simply-connected]]), and let $\alpha$ be a $C^1$ one-form on $U$ with $d\alpha=0$ ([[def-closed-and-exact-differential-forms]]); here closedness of a $C^1$ one-form means that in an inertial chart ([[def-inertial-frame-and-inertial-chart]]) one has $\alpha=\sum_i a_i\,dx^i$ with $\partial_i a_j=\partial_j a_i$, the exterior derivative being understood by this coefficient formula ([[def-exterior-derivative-by-the-invariant-vector-field-formula]], [[thm-local-coordinate-formula-for-the-exterior-derivative]]). Then:

**Conventions (what the objects mean here).** Fix one inertial chart $x:A\to\mathbb R^4$ and put $\Omega:=x(U)\subseteq\mathbb R^4$; by [[lem-affine-minkowski-charts-form-a-smooth-atlas]] the chart $x$ is a diffeomorphism of $A$ onto $\mathbb R^4$ carrying the model's topology, and every other inertial chart $x'$ satisfies $x'=M^{-1}(x-b)$ for an invertible matrix $M$ and a vector $b$. The $C^1$ one-form $\alpha$ is represented in the chart as $\alpha=\sum_i a_i\,dx^i$ with coefficient functions $a_i:\Omega\to\mathbb R$ of class $C^1$; write $A:=(a_1,a_2,a_3,a_4):\Omega\to\mathbb R^4$ for the coefficient field, so that $A$ is $C^1$ and closedness reads $\partial_i a_j=\partial_j a_i$ on $\Omega$. For a piecewise-$C^1$ path $\gamma$ in $U$ the integral is $\int_\gamma\alpha:=\int_{x\circ\gamma}A\cdot d\mathbf r$, the vector-field line integral of [[def-scalar-and-vector-line-integrals-along-piecewise-c1-paths]]. For a $C^1$ function $F:U\to\mathbb R$ with $\tilde F:=F\circ x^{-1}$, the differential $dF$ is the one-form whose chart coefficients are the partial derivatives $\partial_i\tilde F$, and $dF=\alpha$ means $\partial_i\tilde F=a_i$ on $\Omega$ for all $i$. Under the transition $x'=M^{-1}(x-b)$ the chain rule gives $a'_j=\sum_i M^i_j a_i$, $\partial_j\tilde F'=\sum_i M^i_j\,\partial_i\tilde F$ and $(x'\circ\gamma)'=M^{-1}(x\circ\gamma)'$, so the integral $\int_\gamma\alpha$ and the identity $dF=\alpha$ do not depend on which inertial chart is used; likewise, $F$ being $C^2$, respectively smooth, is chart-independent. It therefore suffices to prove the following statement about the open set $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^4$ and the $C^1$ closed field $A$: every closed piecewise-$C^1$ path in $\Omega$ has zero $A$-integral, the $A$-integral is path-independent on $\Omega$, and there is a $C^2$ function $\tilde F$ on $\Omega$ with $\nabla\tilde F=A$ which can be taken smooth when $A$ is smooth.

**Given:** An oriented time-oriented affine Minkowski space $(A,V,\eta,C^+)$ ([[def-sr-affine-minkowski-model]]), a nonempty open subset $U\subseteq A$ that is path-connected and simply connected ([[def-simply-connected]]) in the topology of [[lem-affine-minkowski-charts-form-a-smooth-atlas]], and a $C^1$ one-form $\alpha$ on $U$ with $d\alpha=0$ in the coefficient sense of the Statement ([[def-closed-and-exact-differential-forms]], [[def-exterior-derivative-by-the-invariant-vector-field-formula]]).

[F1] An inertial chart $x:A\to\mathbb R^4$ is a diffeomorphism of $A$ onto $\mathbb R^4$ for the model's topology (which is independent of the chart), the transitions between inertial charts are the affine bijections $x'=M^{-1}(x-b)$, and every inertial chart belongs to the same smooth structure ([[def-inertial-frame-and-inertial-chart]], [[lem-affine-minkowski-charts-form-a-smooth-atlas]], [[def-sr-affine-minkowski-model]]).

[F1] An inertial chart $x:A\to\mathbb R^4$ is a diffeomorphism of $A$ onto $\mathbb R^4$ for the model's topology (which is independent of the chart), the transitions between inertial charts are the affine bijections $x'=M^{-1}(x-b)$, and every inertial chart belongs to the same smooth structure ([[def-inertial-frame-and-inertial-chart]], [[lem-affine-minkowski-charts-form-a-smooth-atlas]], [[def-sr-affine-minkowski-model]]).

1.1 Fix an inertial chart $x$ and put $\Omega:=x(U)$; by [F1] the chart is a diffeomorphism onto $\mathbb R^4$, so $\Omega$ is a nonempty open subset of $\mathbb R^4$, and because $x|_U:U\to\Omega$ is a homeomorphism it induces a bijection between the continuous loops at $p$ in $U$ and those at $x(p)$ in $\Omega$ and a bijection between homotopies relative to the endpoints of such loops (via composition with $x$ and $x^{-1}$); hence $\Omega$ is path-connected and $\pi_1(\Omega,u)$ has exactly one element for every $u\in\Omega$ by [F2]. Write $\alpha=\sum_i a_i\,dx^i$ in the chart with $C^1$ coefficients $a_i$ and $\partial_i a_j=\partial_j a_i$, set $A:=(a_1,\dots,a_4)$, and recall from the conventions of the Statement that $\int_\gamma\alpha=\int_{x\circ\gamma}A\cdot d\mathbf r$ for piecewise-$C^1$ $\gamma$, that $dF=\alpha$ means $\partial_i\tilde F=a_i$ for $\tilde F=F\circ x^{-1}$, and that these interpretations are invariant under a change of inertial chart, by the transition formula $x'=M^{-1}(x-b)$ of [F1] together with the chain rule of [F9] applied to $a'_j=\sum_i M^i_j a_i$, $\partial_j\tilde F'=\sum_i M^i_j\partial_i\tilde F$ and $(x'\circ\gamma)'=M^{-1}(x\circ\gamma)'$; consequently the Statement follows once it is proved for the open set $\Omega$ and the $C^1$ closed field $A$ on it that (i) every closed piecewise-$C^1$ path in $\Omega$ has zero $A$-integral, (ii) the $A$-integral is path-independent on $\Omega$, and (iii) there is a $C^2$ function on $\Omega$ with gradient $A$, smooth when $A$ is smooth. Let $x:I\to A$ be a $C^2$ future timelike worldline with four-velocity $U$ and four-acceleration $A$ ([[def-sr-four-velocity-and-four-acceleration]], [[def-sr-regular-causal-curve-and-worldline]]), let $\tau_0\in I$ and $X_0\in V$. Then there is exactly one $C^1$ field $X:I\to V$ along $x$ with $D_{\mathrm{FW}}X/d\tau=0$ and $X(\tau_0)=X_0$ ([[def-sr-fermi-walker-transport]]); if $x$ is $C^k$ with $k\ge2$ then $X$ is $C^{k-1}$. The map $X_0\mapsto X$, from $V$ to the $C^1$ fields along $x$ satisfying the transport equation, is linear. Consequently, for every tetrad $(E_0(\tau_0),\dots,E_3(\tau_0))$ at $x(\tau_0)$ with $E_0(\tau_0)=U(\tau_0)/c$ there is a unique tuple of Fermi–Walker transported fields with those initial values; whether that tuple remains a tetrad at every time is proved in the following item.

**Given:** A $C^2$ future timelike worldline $x:I\to A$ with four-velocity $U$ and four-acceleration $A$ ([[def-sr-four-velocity-and-four-acceleration]]), a parameter $\tau_0\in I$, an initial vector $X_0\in V$, and the Fermi–Walker transport equation of [[def-sr-fermi-walker-transport]].

[F1] The Fermi–Walker derivative is $D_{\mathrm{FW}}X/d\tau=X'/\tau'-c^{-2}\bigl(\eta(A,X)U-\eta(U,X)A\bigr)$, where $X'$ is the ordinary $V$-valued derivative of the field $X$ along $x$, equal to the covariant derivative along $x$ in the flat model ([[def-sr-fermi-walker-transport]], [[def-flat-covariant-derivative-on-affine-minkowski-space]] clause (d), [[def-vector-valued-derivative-and-integral]]).

[F2] In the ordered basis $(e_0,\dots,e_3)$ of an inertial frame, write $X=X^ae_a$, $U=U^ae_a$, $A=A^ae_a$ and $A_b=\eta_{bc}A^c$, $U_b=\eta_{bc}U^c$. Then $\eta(A,X)=A_bX^b$ and $\eta(U,X)=U_bX^b$, and the transport equation $D_{\mathrm{FW}}X/d\tau=0$ is equivalent to the linear system $X'^a=\tau'M^a{}_bX^b$ with $M^a{}_b=c^{-2}\bigl(U^aA_b-A^aU_b\bigr)$ ([[def-sr-fermi-walker-transport]], [[def-ck-tensor-field-on-minkowski-space]], [[def-inertial-frame-and-inertial-chart]]).

[F3] If $x$ is $C^k$ with $k\ge2$, then $U$ is $C^{k-1}$ and $A$ is $C^{k-2}$: $U=c\,x'/\sqrt{-\eta(x',x')}$ and $\tau'=c^{-1}\sqrt{-\eta(x',x')}$ are quotients of $C^{k-1}$ functions with nonvanishing denominator, and $A=U'/\tau'$ is a quotient of $C^{k-2}$ functions ([[def-sr-four-velocity-and-four-acceleration]], [[def-ck-and-multi-index-notation-in-several-variables]], [[thm-algebra-of-derivatives]]). Consequently, if $x$ is $C^2$ then $M$ and $C:=\tau'M$ are continuous, and if $x$ is $C^k$ then both are $C^{k-2}$ because $\tau'$ is $C^{k-1}$.

5.2 The initial-tetrad clause: let $E_0(\tau_0),\dots,E_3(\tau_0)$ be a tetrad at $x(\tau_0)$ with $E_0(\tau_0)=U(\tau_0)/c$ ([[def-sr-chart-tetrad-and-congruence-distinction]]). By steps 4.1 and 3.1, for each $a$ there is exactly one $C^1$ Fermi–Walker transported field $E_a:I\to V$ along $x$ with $E_a(\tau_0)$ equal to the prescribed value. For $a=0$ the field $U/c$ is $C^1$, satisfies $D_{\mathrm{FW}}(U/c)/d\tau=0$ by clause (b) of [[def-sr-fermi-walker-transport]], and has the same initial value $U(\tau_0)/c$; by the uniqueness of step 3.1, $E_0=U/c$. Hence there is a unique tuple of Fermi–Walker transported fields with the prescribed initial values, and its time component is the four-velocity up to the factor $1/c$. [step 3.1, step 4.1]

[L3] An inertial frame is a tuple $(o;e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3)$ with $o\in A$ and $(e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3)$ an $\eta$-orthonormal basis of $V$ with $\eta(e_a,e_b)=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)_{ab}$, whose first vector $e_0$ lies in $C^+$ and which is positively oriented; its chart is $x(r)=E^{-1}(r-o)$ with $E(u)=\sum_a u^ae_a$, and in particular $x(r)-x(s)=E^{-1}(r-s)$ ([[def-inertial-frame-and-inertial-chart]]).

Let $c > 0$ and $\alpha > 0$, set $R := c^2/\alpha$, and let $(A,V,\eta,C^+)$ be the affine Minkowski space with an inertial chart $x = (x^0,x^1,x^2,x^3)$, $x^0 = c t$ ([[def-sr-affine-minkowski-model]], [[def-inertial-frame-and-inertial-chart]]). Let $x: \mathbb R \to A$ be the curve $x(\tau) := x^{-1}(R \sinh \theta, R \cosh \theta, 0, 0)$, where $\theta := \alpha \tau/c$.

(a) **Regularity, causal character and parametrization.** $x$ is $C^\infty$, and $x'(\tau) = c(\cosh \theta, \sinh \theta, 0, 0)$ is future timelike for every $\tau$ ([[def-causal-classification-of-lorentz-vectors]], [[def-time-orientation-and-future-causal-sets]]), so $x$ is a future timelike worldline ([[def-sr-regular-causal-curve-and-worldline]]). Since $\eta(x',x') = -c^2$ is constant, the parameter $\tau$ is a proper-time parameter of the curve: the proper-time function $\tau$ of [[def-sr-proper-time]] satisfies $\tau(b) - \tau(a) = b - a$ for all $a < b$ in $\mathbb R$ ([[def-sr-proper-time]], [[lem-sr-proper-time-parametrization]]), and the four-velocity is $U := dx/d\tau = c(\cosh \theta, \sinh \theta, 0, 0)$ with $\eta(U,U) = -c^2$ ([[def-sr-four-velocity-and-four-acceleration]], [[thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition]] (a)).

(c) **Rindler flow line.** Let $\Phi(\theta,\rho,y,z) := (\rho \sinh \theta, \rho \cosh \theta, y, z)$ on $\mathbb R \times (0,\infty) \times \mathbb R^2$ and let $n := \rho^{-1} \partial_\theta$ be the Rindler congruence of [[thm-sr-fermi-walker-and-rigid-observer-examples]] (b), whose pullback metric is $-\rho^2 d\theta^2 + d\rho^2 + dy^2 + dz^2$ and whose congruence acceleration $a_{\mathrm{cg}} := \nabla_n n$ is $\rho^{-1} \partial_\rho$, with $\eta(a_{\mathrm{cg}},a_{\mathrm{cg}}) = \rho^{-2}$ ([[def-flat-covariant-derivative-on-affine-minkowski-space]], [[def-sr-observer-congruence-and-kinematics]]). Then $x$ is exactly the flow line $\Phi(\cdot, R, 0, 0)$ reparametrized by $\theta = \alpha \tau/c$, and along $x$ one has $A = c^2 a_{\mathrm{cg}}$: the four-acceleration of the worldline is $c^2$ times the congruence acceleration, and $\eta(a_{\mathrm{cg}},a_{\mathrm{cg}}) = 1/R^2 = \alpha^2/c^4$ on the flow line $\rho = R$.

**Given:** The affine Minkowski space $(A,V,\eta,C^+)$ with fixed $c>0$; an inertial chart $x=(x^0,x^1,x^2,x^3)$ with $x^0=ct$ and orthonormal basis $(e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3)$ ([[def-inertial-frame-and-inertial-chart]]); $\alpha>0$, $R=c^2/\alpha$, $\theta=\alpha\tau/c$, and the curve $x(\tau)=x^{-1}(R\sinh\theta,R\cosh\theta,0,0)$ for $\tau\in\mathbb R$.

[F1] Inertial frames and charts: for every event $o$ and every $\eta$-orthonormal ordered basis $(f_0,f_1,f_2,f_3)$ of $V$ with future first vector and positive orientation, $(o;f_0,\dots,f_3)$ is an inertial frame; its chart is $x(r)=E^{-1}(r-o)$ with $E(u)=\sum_a u^ae_a$ the frame's linear isomorphism, and every vector $u$ has unique coordinates $u=u^0e_0+u_s$, $u_s\in S=\operatorname{span}(e_1,e_2,e_3)$ ([[def-inertial-frame-and-inertial-chart]], [[lem-future-oriented-inertial-frames-exist]]).

[F2] Cone coordinates: in an inertial frame with first vector in $C^+$ one has $C^+=\{u:u^0>|u_s|\}$ and $C^-=\{u:u^0<-|u_s|\}$, and $\eta(u,u)=-(u^0)^2+|u_s|^2$; the restriction of $\eta$ to $S$ is positive definite, $(e_1,e_2,e_3)$ is orthonormal for it, and $|z|^2=\delta(z,z)$ for $z\in S$ ([[lem-timelike-cone-has-two-convex-components]], [[def-time-orientation-and-future-causal-sets]], [[def-spatial-euclidean-structure-of-an-inertial-frame]]).

[F3] The passive boost $B(\beta)$ is defined for every parameter $\beta\in\mathbb{R}^3$ with $|\beta|<1$ ([[def-lorentz-boost]]); it is a proper orthochronous Lorentz map with inverse $B(-\beta)$ ([[lem-boost-is-proper-orthochronous-with-inverse]], [[def-lorentz-map-and-lorentz-group]]); and if $u$ is future timelike with $\eta(u,u)=-1$ and coordinates $(u^0,u_s)$, then the parameter $\beta:=u_s/u^0$ satisfies $|\beta|<1$ and $B(\beta)u=f_0$, where $f_0$ is the first vector of the frame used for the coordinates ([[lem-boost-is-proper-orthochronous-with-inverse]] (iv)).

[F4] Lorentz maps preserve the metric and the orientation class: for a linear Lorentz map $L$ one has $\eta(Lv,Lw)=\eta(v,w)$ for all $v,w$; the composition and the inverse of Lorentz maps are Lorentz maps, and the proper orthochronous ones form a group; if $L$ is proper, then the oriented volume form $\epsilon$ of [[def-oriented-minkowski-volume-form]] is preserved, $\epsilon(Lv_0,\dots,Lv_3)=\epsilon(v_0,\dots,v_3)$; and $\epsilon$ takes the value $1$ on every positively oriented $\eta$-orthonormal basis, so a tuple of four vectors with $\epsilon$-value $1$ is positively oriented ([[lem-lorentz-map-preserves-metric-and-causal-structure]], [[lem-volume-form-is-independent-of-the-oriented-frame]]).

[F1] Inertial frames and charts: at every event $o\in A$ there is an inertial frame $(o;e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3)$; its ordered basis is $\eta$-orthonormal with $\eta(e_a,e_b)=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)_{ab}$, its first vector $e_0$ lies in $C^+$, and $E(u):=\sum_a u^ae_a$ is a linear isomorphism $E:\mathbb{R}^4\to V$, so every vector $u\in V$ has unique coordinates $u=u^0e_0+u_s$ with $u_s=u^1e_1+u^2e_2+u^3e_3$ ([[lem-future-oriented-inertial-frames-exist]], [[def-inertial-frame-and-inertial-chart]]).

[F3] Spatial and bilinear structure: for a frame of [F1], the spatial three-space $S:=\operatorname{span}(e_1,e_2,e_3)=\{z\in V:\eta(e_0,z)=0\}$ carries the restriction $\delta:=\eta|_S$, which is positive definite, and $|z|:=\sqrt{\delta(z,z)}$ is a norm on $S$ with $(e_1,e_2,e_3)$ a $\delta$-orthonormal basis; since $\eta$ is bilinear, for all $u=u^0e_0+u_s$ and $u'=u'^0e_0+u'_s$ one has $\eta(u,u')=-u^0u'^0+\delta(u_s,u'_s)$, and in particular $\eta(u,u)=-(u^0)^2+|u_s|^2$ ([[def-spatial-euclidean-structure-of-an-inertial-frame]], [[def-lorentz-form-and-inertia]]).

Let $\Omega\subseteq A$ be a nonempty open set with an inertial chart $x$, let $K>0$, let $V:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$ be smooth and let $\varphi:\Omega\to\mathbb R$ be a smooth real scalar field ([[def-ck-tensor-field-on-minkowski-space]]). For every smooth compactly supported $h:\Omega\to\mathbb R$ define the first variation $$\delta S(\varphi)[h]:=-\frac{K}{c}\int_\Omega\Big(\eta^{ab}\partial_a\varphi\,\partial_bh+V'(\varphi)h\Big)\,d^4x,$$ a finite Riemann integral by compact support of $h$ ([[lem-sr-compact-variation-and-fundamental-lemma]]\,(c)). Then (a) $\delta S(\varphi)[h]=\dfrac{K}{c}\int_\Omega\big(\Box\varphi-V'(\varphi)\big)h\,d^4x$, where $\Box\varphi:=\eta^{ab}\partial_a\partial_b\varphi$; (b) $\delta S(\varphi)[h]=0$ for every such $h$ if and only if $\Box\varphi=V'(\varphi)$ on $\Omega$. The equation in (b) is called the scalar-field equation of this model. The statement is the first variation of the action on compactly supported variations; it asserts nothing about convergence of $S$ on unbounded domains, no boundary term, no dynamics beyond the equivalence in (b) and no empirical fact. No choice principle is used. Precisely, with $L(\phi):=\tfrac12\eta^{ab}\partial_a\phi\partial_b\phi+V(\phi)$, define the relative action $S_h(s):=-(K/c)\int_\Omega[L(\varphi+sh)-L(\varphi)]\,d^4x$. Its integrand has support in $\operatorname{supp}h$, so it is defined for every real $s$ even when either background action diverges; $S_h\prime(0)=\delta S(\varphi)[h]$.

**Given:** The affine Minkowski model $(A,V,\eta,C^+)$ with a fixed inertial chart $x$ and its coordinate partial derivatives $\partial_a$ ([[def-sr-affine-minkowski-model]], [[def-lorentz-form-and-inertia]], [[def-directional-and-partial-derivatives]]), a nonempty open $\Omega\subseteq A$, a numerical constant $K>0$, a smooth $V:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$, a smooth real scalar field $\varphi:\Omega\to\mathbb R$ ([[def-ck-tensor-field-on-minkowski-space]]), and smooth compactly supported real $h:\Omega\to\mathbb R$. In the inertial chart the metric components are the constant matrices $\eta_{ab}=\eta^{ab}=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$, with $\eta^{ab}=\eta^{ba}$ ([[def-inertial-frame-and-inertial-chart]]). We write $\Box\varphi:=\eta^{ab}\partial_a\partial_b\varphi$ and $L(\phi):=\tfrac12\eta^{ab}\partial_a\phi\partial_b\phi+V(\phi)$ for a smooth scalar function $\phi$.

[F1] Compactly supported differentiation under the integral sign: if $F:(-s_0,s_0)\times\Omega\to\mathbb R$ is continuous with continuous $\partial_sF$ and there is a compact $K\Subset\Omega$ with $F(s,z)=0$ for $z\notin K$ and all $s$, then $s\mapsto\int_\Omega F(s,z)\,d^4z$ is $C^1$ on $(-s_0,s_0)$ with derivative $\int_\Omega\partial_sF(s,z)\,d^4z$. ([[lem-sr-compact-variation-and-fundamental-lemma]]\,(c))

[F2] Compact-support integration by parts: if $f:\Omega\to\mathbb R$ is $C^1$ and compactly supported and $g:\Omega\to\mathbb R$ is $C^1$, then for each $a$, $\int_\Omega(\partial_af)g\,d^4x=-\int_\Omega f(\partial_ag)\,d^4x$. ([[lem-sr-compact-variation-and-fundamental-lemma]]\,(b))

[F3] Fundamental lemma: if $g:\Omega\to\mathbb R$ is continuous and $\int_\Omega g\psi\,d^4x=0$ for every smooth compactly supported $\psi:\Omega\to\mathbb R$, then $g=0$ on $\Omega$. ([[lem-sr-compact-variation-and-fundamental-lemma]]\,(a))

[L1] An inertial frame is a tuple $(o;e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3)$ with $o\in A$ and $(e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3)$ an $\eta$-orthonormal, future, positively oriented ordered basis of $V$; its chart is $x(r)=E^{-1}(r-o)$ with $E(u)=\sum_a u^a e_a$, and the components $x^a(r)$ are the inertial coordinates of $r$ ([[def-inertial-frame-and-inertial-chart]]).

[L2] In an $\eta$-orthonormal basis with coordinates $v=v^0e_0+\cdots+v^3e_3$ one has $\eta(v,v)=-(v^0)^2+|v_s|^2$, where $|v_s|=\sqrt{(v^1)^2+(v^2)^2+(v^3)^2}$ is the Euclidean norm of the spatial part; for a fixed inertial frame the spatial part $S=\operatorname{span}(e_1,e_2,e_3)$ carries the positive-definite form $\delta=\eta|_S$ and the norm $|\cdot|$ ([[lem-timelike-cone-has-two-convex-components]], [[def-spatial-euclidean-structure-of-an-inertial-frame]]).

[L4] For $\beta\in\mathbb R^3$ with $|\beta|<1$ the passive boost is the linear map $B(\beta):V\to V$ whose action on coordinates is $x'^0=\gamma(x^0-\beta\cdot x)$, $x'=x+\frac{\gamma-1}{|\beta|^2}(\beta\cdot x)\beta-\gamma\beta x^0$ for $\beta\ne 0$ and $B(0)=\mathrm{id}$, where $\gamma=(1-|\beta|^2)^{-1/2}$ and $\beta\cdot x$ is the Euclidean scalar product of $\beta$ with the spatial coordinates of $x$ ([[def-lorentz-boost]], [[def-euclidean-inner-product]]).

**Given:** The oriented time-oriented affine Minkowski space $(A,V,\eta,C^+)$ of [[def-sr-affine-minkowski-model]] with the postulates [[post-sr-inertial-covariance]], [[post-sr-ideal-clocks-and-light]] and [[post-sr-causal-signal-propagation]] adopted as physical assumptions, an inertial chart $x$ with $x^0=ct$ ([[def-inertial-frame-and-inertial-chart]], [[def-sr-si-units-and-coordinate-conventions]]), and events $p,q,r\in A$.

[L1] Causal signal restriction: a signal is information or a physical marker correlating a prepared operation at the emission event with an observation at the reception event within the model, and the model admits a transmission carrying a signal from $p$ to $q$ only if $q\in J^+(p)$, that is only if $q-p$ is zero or future causal; ideal vacuum light signals are the future null boundary case; the restriction is adopted, not derived, and not an empirical claim; kinematic patterns from independent prearranged mechanisms are explicitly not restricted ([[post-sr-causal-signal-propagation]]).

[L2] Criterion and cone description: $\overline{C^+}$ is a convex cone with $\overline{C^+}\cap\overline{C^-}=\{0\}$; for $D=x(q)-x(p)$, $q\in J^+(p)$ iff $D^0\ge|D_s|$; $q\in I^+(p)$ iff $D^0>|D_s|$; every nonzero element of $\overline{C^+}$ has $D^0>0$; sums of finitely many elements of $\overline{C^+}$ lie in $\overline{C^+}$, and if one summand lies in $C^+$ the sum lies in $C^+$ ([[lem-sr-future-causal-sums-and-inertial-coordinate-criterion]]).

[L3] Spacelike pairs: for $q-p$ spacelike one has $|D^0|<|D_s|$ in every inertial chart, and there are inertial frames whose charts give $x^0(q)-x^0(p)$ either sign and inertial frames of simultaneity ([[lem-sr-spacelike-pairs-have-frame-dependent-time-order]]).

[L4] Causal loops and covariance: if $p\le q$ and $q\le p$ then $p=q$; and for every proper orthochronous affine Lorentz map $F$ one has $F(J^+(p))=J^+(F(p))$, $F(I^+(p))=I^+(F(p))$, and $p\le q$ iff $F(p)\le F(q)$ ([[thm-sr-future-cone-and-flat-domain-of-dependence]]).

[L5] Inertial covariance: the equations of the specified model are covariant under the affine maps with proper orthochronous Lorentz linear part, and those maps are the inertial changes of description ([[post-sr-inertial-covariance]], [[def-lorentz-map-and-lorentz-group]]).

[L6] Interval and cone invariance: the causal classification of a displacement and, for causal displacements, the future/past alternative are independent of the inertial chart, and the interval computed from coordinates is chart independent ([[pthm-sr-interval-and-cone-invariance]], [[lem-lorentz-map-preserves-metric-and-causal-structure]], [[thm-sr-proper-orthochronous-lorentz-algebra]], [[def-causal-classification-of-lorentz-vectors]]).

By the covariance clause of [L4] one has $F(J^+(p))=J^+(F(p))$, $F(I^+(p))=I^+(F(p))$ and $p\le q$ iff $F(p)\le F(q)$ for every proper orthochronous affine Lorentz map $F$, and by [L5] these maps are exactly the inertial changes of description of the model. Since [L1] admits a signal from $p$ to $q$ only when $q\in J^+(p)$, the condition is preserved under every change of description; [L6] records independently that the causal classification and the future/past alternative of the specified model are chart independent, in agreement with [[pthm-sr-interval-and-cone-invariance]]. **Given:** The adopted postulates [[post-sr-inertial-covariance]], [[post-sr-ideal-clocks-and-light]] and [[post-sr-free-trajectories-and-clock-hypothesis]]; the SI conventions of [[def-sr-si-units-and-coordinate-conventions]]; and a $C^{1}$ future timelike worldline $x : I \to A$ that is the history of an ideal clock, $C^{2}$ where acceleration is used.

[A1] Free trajectories: a massive test particle subject to no interaction has as its worldline a straight future timelike line $x(s) = p+(s-s_0)v$ with $v$ future timelike; interactions and force laws are not part of the assumption ([[post-sr-free-trajectories-and-clock-hypothesis]], clause (i)).

[A2] Clock hypothesis: an ideal clock carried along a future timelike worldline reads, between parameter values, the proper-time difference of [[def-sr-proper-time]] ([[post-sr-free-trajectories-and-clock-hypothesis]], clause (ii); [[post-sr-ideal-clocks-and-light]], clause (i)).

[A3] The model's postulates hold: the affine Minkowski space is the spacetime, and the model equations are covariant under inertial changes of description ([[post-sr-inertial-covariance]]); ideal clocks and ideal light are as stated in [[post-sr-ideal-clocks-and-light]].
[L1] Units ([[def-sr-si-units-and-coordinate-conventions]]): the four-velocity $U = dx/d\tau$ has unit m/s and the four-acceleration m/s$^{2}$; the interval carries m$^{2}$.

[L2] Four-velocity and four-acceleration ([[def-sr-four-velocity-and-four-acceleration]]): $U = x'/\tau'$ and $A = U'/\tau'$; the four-velocity of the observer's own straight worldline with future unit timelike $n$ is $cn$.

[L3] Mathematical content ([[thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition]]): $\eta(U,U) = -c^{2}$; $\eta(U,A) = 0$ and $A$ zero or spacelike when $x$ is $C^{2}$; for future unit timelike $n$ and $u = U/c$, with $\gamma = -\eta(n,u)$, $\gamma \ge 1$, $|w| = c\sqrt{1-\gamma^{-2}} < c$ for $w = c\,h(u)/\gamma$, and $\gamma = 1$ if and only if $u = n$; $w$ is the velocity of a worldline with four-velocity $cu$ relative to $n$.

[L4] Proper-time definition ([[def-sr-proper-time]], [[def-sr-regular-causal-curve-and-worldline]]): $\tau' = c^{-1}\sqrt{-\eta(x',x')}$, and for the straight worldline $x(s) = p+(s-s_0)v$ the difference quotients are identically $v$, so $x' = v$ and $\tau' = c^{-1}\sqrt{-\eta(v,v)}$ is constant.

- **What is assumed and what is derived.** Clauses (i) and (iv) rest on the adopted free-trajectory and clock assumptions; clauses (ii), (iii) and (v) are the mathematical content of [[thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition]] read through the model's interpretation. The theorem asserts what follows from the adopted model, not that ideal clocks or free particles exist as described in nature.

Adopt [[post-sr-inertial-covariance]] and [[post-sr-ideal-clocks-and-light]] and the SI conventions of [[def-sr-si-units-and-coordinate-conventions]] ($x^0 = c t$). Let $x = (x^0,x^1,x^2,x^3)$ be the chart of an inertial frame ([[def-inertial-frame-and-inertial-chart]]). Fix $R > 0$, a real $\Omega$ with $|\Omega| R < c$, a real $x^3_0$ and a real $\phi_0$, and put $\gamma := (1 - \Omega^2 R^2/c^2)^{-1/2}$. A rigidly rotating circular ring of radius $R$ and height $x^3_0$ about the $x^3$-axis, with angular velocity $\Omega$, has material worldlines

$\eta(n,n) = -1$, and four-velocity $U = c n = \gamma\,\partial_t|_{\varphi}$, $\eta(U,U) = -c^2$, where $\varphi := \phi - \Omega t$ is the rotating angular label of the ring material points; it is an unparametrized flow line of the rigid-rotation congruence $n = \gamma(r)\,[\partial_0 + (\Omega/c)(-x^2\partial_1 + x^1\partial_2)]$ restricted to $r = R$, and its proper time $\tau$ and the chart time $t$ satisfy $d\tau = dt/\gamma$, so $\tau = t/\gamma + \tau_0$ for an arbitrary proper-time origin $\tau_0$ on this worldline ([[thm-sr-fermi-walker-and-rigid-observer-examples]] (c), [[def-sr-proper-time]], [[lem-sr-proper-time-parametrization]]).

(iv) **Relation to the ring rest-synchronization holonomy.** On the fixed-height timelike cylinder $C = \{r = R,\ x^3 = x^3_0\}$, material worldlines have constant rotating label. Its rest lines instead vary $\varphi$ on an angular lift and satisfy $dt/d\varphi = \Omega R^2/(c^2 - \Omega^2R^2)$, being integral curves of $\partial_\varphi + [\Omega R^2/(c^2 - \Omega^2R^2)]\,\partial_t$; for $\Omega = 0$ they are $t = \text{constant}$ circles; one circuit $\varphi \to \varphi + 2 \pi$ has the chart-time holonomy $\Delta t_h = 2 \pi \Omega R^2/(c^2 - \Omega^2R^2) = (t_1 - t_2)/2$ and the receiver proper-time holonomy $\Delta \tau_h = \Delta t_h/\gamma = 2 \pi \Omega R^2/(c^2 \sqrt{1 - \Omega^2R^2/c^2}) = (1/2)(t_1 - t_2)/\gamma$, exactly half of the detector proper-time difference of (iii); for $\Omega = 0$ both holonomies vanish. The ambient three-dimensional rest distribution of the rotating congruence is nowhere integrable for $\Omega \neq 0$, so no ambient rest-simultaneity hypersurface exists, while the one-dimensional rest distribution restricted to the fixed-height cylinder $C$ is locally integrable and has the global holonomy just computed, nonvanishing exactly when $\Omega \neq 0$; the return-time computation of (iii) uses only the guided null curves and the material worldline and does not use either integrability property ([[thm-sr-fermi-walker-and-rigid-observer-examples]] (c), [[thm-sr-local-congruence-adapted-charts-and-frobenius]]).

(v) **Scope.** All quantities are conditional model computations for the specified ring, guide, signal and detector idealizations. The guided-signal curves are an adopted device model: the ideal vacuum light rays of [[post-sr-ideal-clocks-and-light]] are straight future null lines and do not circulate around the ring by themselves, and no assertion is made about optical fibers, refractive media, dispersion, absorption, finite resolution, apparatus calibration, interference phase or wave optics, or about one-way synchronization conventions between distinct ring observers; no measurement outcome, statistical inference or empirical claim is made, the values of $R$ and $\Omega$ are parameters and not measured quantities, and no choice principle is used.

[L1] Ideal clocks read the proper time of their worldline, and ideal vacuum light rays are the future null straight lines with coordinate speed $c$ in every inertial chart ([[post-sr-ideal-clocks-and-light]]).

[L2] In every inertial chart the coordinates are $x^0=ct$, the matrix of $\eta$ is $\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$ with dimensionless entries, and the interval carries $\mathrm m^2$ ([[def-sr-si-units-and-coordinate-conventions]], [[def-inertial-frame-and-inertial-chart]]).

[L3] Points of $A$ are determined by their inertial coordinates, and vector components are read in the orthonormal basis $(e_a)$ ([[def-inertial-frame-and-inertial-chart]], [[def-sr-affine-minkowski-model]]).

[L4] A curve $x:I\to A$ is differentiable precisely when its coordinate representation is, its tangent is the corresponding $V$-vector, and it is $C^k$ when that representation is; at a regular point the causal character and future direction of the curve are those of its tangent ([[def-sr-regular-causal-curve-and-worldline]] (a),(b)).

[L5] Causal classification: timelike means $\eta(v,v)<0$, null means $v\neq0$ and $\eta(v,v)=0$, and each nonzero causal vector is future or past but not both; $C^+=\{v:v^0>|v_s|\}$ and $\bar C^+=\{v:v^0\ge|v_s|\}$ in every inertial chart ([[def-causal-classification-of-lorentz-vectors]], [[def-time-orientation-and-future-causal-sets]], [[lem-sr-future-causal-sums-and-inertial-coordinate-criterion]] (a)).

[L6] Four-velocity: $U=x'/\tau'=cx'/\sqrt{-\eta(x',x')}$ with $\eta(U,U)=-c^2$ along a $C^1$ future timelike worldline, and for a congruence flow line with tangent $x'=cn$ the four-velocity is $cn$ ([[def-sr-four-velocity-and-four-acceleration]] (a),(c), [[thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition]] (a)).

[L7] Proper time: for a $C^1$ future timelike worldline, $\tau(b)-\tau(a)=c^{-1}\int_a^b\sqrt{-\eta(x',x')}\,du$, and the proper-time reparametrization is $C^1$ with tangent $x'/\tau'$ ([[def-sr-proper-time]], [[lem-sr-proper-time-parametrization]] (i),(iii),(iv)).

[L10] Rigid rotation and the ring: on the timelike region $r^2<c^2/\Omega^2$ the field $n=\gamma(r)[\partial_0+(\Omega/c)(-x^2\partial_1+x^1\partial_2)]$ is a smooth future unit timelike Born-rigid congruence with nowhere-zero vorticity for $\Omega\neq0$; on the ring cylinder $r=R$, $x^3=\text{const}$, the induced metric is $-(c^2-\Omega^2R^2)dt^2+2\Omega R^2\,dt\,d\varphi+R^2d\varphi^2$, the ring observer $\phi=\phi_0+\Omega t$ has $n=\gamma(R)(1,-(\Omega R/c)\sin\phi,(\Omega R/c)\cos\phi,0)$, the one-dimensional rest distribution is locally integrable with $dt/d\varphi=\Omega R^2/(c^2-\Omega^2R^2)$, one positive circuit has signed chart-time offset $\Delta t=2\pi\Omega R^2/(c^2-\Omega^2R^2)$, and for $\Omega=0$ the ring is inertial with rest lines $t=\text{const}$ ([[thm-sr-fermi-walker-and-rigid-observer-examples]] (c)).

[L11] Frobenius: the ambient rest distribution of an observer congruence is integrable on an open set exactly where its vorticity vanishes; a locally integrable rank-one cylinder distribution is unaffected by the ambient obstruction ([[thm-sr-local-congruence-adapted-charts-and-frobenius]] (iii), [[def-sr-observer-congruence-and-kinematics]] (c),(d)).

Let $x$ be an inertial chart, let $\bar K$ be a closed spatial box and $s_1<s_2$, and let $T$ be the total stress-energy tensor of a system in the situation of [[post-sr-matter-isolation-and-total-stress-energy]]: $T$ is $C^1$ and symmetric on a neighbourhood of $[s_1,s_2]\times\bar K$, satisfies $\partial_aT^{ab}=0$ there (for the adopted models this is the conclusion of [[pthm-sr-local-stress-energy-conservation]]; for any other system it is an explicit premise), and satisfies the zero side-flux condition $T^{ib}=0$ on the spatial faces for $i=1,2,3$. Put $Q^b(s):=\int_{\bar K}T^{0b}(s,x)\,d^3x$ and $P^b:=Q^b/c$. Then: (a) $Q^b(s)$ is finite for every $s\in[s_1,s_2]$ and $Q^b(s_1)=Q^b(s_2)$; (b) consequently $P^b$ is independent of $s\in[s_1,s_2]$; if $P$ is future timelike, its invariant mass $\sqrt{-\eta(P,P)}/c$ is independent of $s$ as well; (c) if the side flux does not vanish, the exact balance is the finite-flux identity of [[thm-sr-stress-balance-and-finite-flux]], and no conservation is asserted; (d) no transformation law for $P^b$ under a change of inertial chart or slicing is asserted: without an admissible-region flux argument, $P^b$ is a chart-component integral and is not claimed to be a four-vector; no noncompact, asymptotic or gravitational-energy statement is made, and the reading of $P^b$ as the system's four-momentum is the model's interpretation of the integral, not a measurement.

**Given:** The affine Minkowski model with inertial chart $x$ ([[def-sr-affine-minkowski-model]], [[def-inertial-frame-and-inertial-chart]]), a closed spatial box $\bar K$, times $s_1<s_2$, and the total tensor $T$ of the isolation premise [[post-sr-matter-isolation-and-total-stress-energy]] with its stated hypotheses; $Q^b(s)=\int_{\bar K}T^{0b}(s,x)\,d^3x$ and $P^b=Q^b/c$; the conservation of $T$ is either the conclusion of [[pthm-sr-local-stress-energy-conservation]] for the adopted models or an explicit premise for any other system.

[F1] Finite-flux theorem: for a $C^1$ symmetric field on a neighbourhood of the box, $Q^b(s)=\int_{\bar K}T^{0b}(s,x)\,d^3x$ is finite and continuous in $s$, and for $c_0\le s_1<s_2\le d_0$ the slice balance $$Q^b(s_2)-Q^b(s_1)=\int_{[s_1,s_2]\times\bar K}\partial_aT^{ab}\,d^4x-\sum_{i=1}^{3}\Big(\int_{[s_1,s_2]\times\bar K_i^+}T^{ib}\,d^3x-\int_{[s_1,s_2]\times\bar K_i^-}T^{ib}\,d^3x\Big)$$ holds; if the force density vanishes on $[s_1,s_2]\times\bar K$ and $T^{ib}=0$ on the side faces, then $Q^b(s_1)=Q^b(s_2)$. ([[thm-sr-stress-balance-and-finite-flux]]\,(b),(c), [[def-sr-stress-energy-tensor-and-force-density]])

[F2] Total four-momentum and invariant mass: for a vector $P=\sum_bP^be_b$ built from a chase of chart components $P^b$, if $P$ is future timelike then its invariant mass is $\sqrt{-\eta(P,P)}/c>0$, and if $P$ is future null the convention assigns mass $0$. ([[def-sr-total-four-momentum-and-invariant-mass]], [[def-causal-classification-of-lorentz-vectors]])

**Given:** The adopted model $(A,V,\eta,C^+)$ with postulates [[post-sr-inertial-covariance]] and [[post-sr-ideal-clocks-and-light]], two inertial frames with charts $x,x'$ of the model, and the events and displacements of the Statement.

[L1] Two inertial charts satisfy $x'(p)=M^{-1}(x(p)-x(o'))$, an affine map with linear part $M^{-1}$, where $M$ is the matrix of the proper orthochronous linear Lorentz map $L$ with $Le_a=e'_a$; $M^{-1}$ is a proper orthochronous Lorentz matrix and the transition maps future causal coordinate vectors to future causal coordinate vectors; conversely every proper orthochronous linear Lorentz map and event give an inertial chart with that transition ([[lem-inertial-chart-transitions-are-affine-lorentz]]).

[L2] For a linear Lorentz map $L$: it preserves $\eta(v,v)$ and the causal character of every nonzero vector and maps the null vectors onto themselves; $L(C^+)$ is one of the components $C^+,C^-$; a proper Lorentz map preserves the oriented volume form, $\epsilon(Lv_0,\dots,Lv_3)=\epsilon(v_0,\dots,v_3)$; the inverse and compositions of Lorentz maps are Lorentz maps; and for the map $-\operatorname{id}$ one has $(-\operatorname{id})(C^+)=C^-$, because $-\operatorname{id}$ is a Lorentz map whose image of $C^+$ is a component different from $C^+$ (no vector of $C^+$ equals its own negative, as $0\notin C^+$) ([[lem-lorentz-map-preserves-metric-and-causal-structure]]).
[L3] Collinear boosts compose by $B(\beta_1e)B(\beta_2e)=B\bigl(\frac{\beta_1+\beta_2}{1+\beta_1\beta_2}e\bigr)$ and commute ([[lem-collinear-boost-composition-and-velocity-addition]]).

[L5] An inertial chart is $x(p)=E^{-1}(p-o)$ for an $\eta$-orthonormal, future, positively oriented basis; in particular coordinate differences transform affinely, and $x^0=ct$ in the SI convention ([[def-inertial-frame-and-inertial-chart]], [[def-sr-si-units-and-coordinate-conventions]]).
[L7] The oriented volume form is $\epsilon(v_0,\dots,v_3)=\det([v_j^a])$, the determinant of the coordinate matrix in an inertial frame ([[def-oriented-minkowski-volume-form]]).

[L8] Adopted: the affine Minkowski model is the spacetime of the framework, and the inertial changes of description are the affine maps whose linear parts are proper orthochronous Lorentz maps; the model equations of the framework are covariant under them ([[post-sr-inertial-covariance]]).

[L9] Adopted: ideal vacuum light rays are exactly the future null straight lines $\{p+\lambda v:\lambda\in\mathbb R\}$ with $v$ future null, and in every inertial chart their spatial coordinate velocity has magnitude $c$ with $x^0=ct$ ([[post-sr-ideal-clocks-and-light]]).

coordinate_mentions.text: $\Delta=x(q)-x(p)$ and $\Delta'=x'(q)-x'(p)$ one has $\Delta'=\Lambda\Delta$

[L1] Two inertial charts satisfy $x'(p)=M^{-1}(x(p)-x(o'))$, an affine map with linear part $M^{-1}$, where $M$ is the matrix of the proper orthochronous linear Lorentz map $L$ with $Le_a=e'_a$; $M^{-1}$ is a proper orthochronous Lorentz matrix and the transition maps future causal coordinate vectors to future causal coordinate vectors; conversely every proper orthochronous linear Lorentz map and event give an inertial chart with that transition ([[lem-inertial-chart-transitions-are-affine-lorentz]]).

1.1 By [L1], the transition is $x'(p)=M^{-1}(x(p)-x(o'))$, the affine map $u\mapsto M^{-1}u-M^{-1}x(o')$ with linear part $\Lambda:=M^{-1}$, the matrix of the linear Lorentz map $L^{-1}$, which is proper orthochronous by [L1] and [L2]. For events $p,q$ the affine formula gives $\Delta'=x'(q)-x'(p)=M^{-1}(x(q)-x(p))=\Lambda\Delta$. Since the matrix $\Lambda$ of the Lorentz map $L^{-1}$ satisfies $\eta_0(\Lambda a,\Lambda b)=\eta_0(a,b)$ for all coordinate columns $a,b$ (the matrix form of the defining Lorentz property), $\eta_0(\Delta',\Delta')=\eta_0(\Lambda\Delta,\Lambda\Delta)=\eta_0(\Delta,\Delta)$, which is exactly $I(p,q)$ by [L4] and [L5]. Hence the interval computed from coordinates does not depend on the inertial chart, proving (i). [L1, L2, L4, L5, algebra]

2.1 The classification of $\Delta$ is read from the sign of $\eta_0(\Delta,\Delta)$: it is timelike when this number is negative, null when it is zero and $\Delta\neq0$, spacelike when it is positive, by [L6] and the coordinate expression $\eta(v,w)=v^{T}\eta_0w$ in an inertial frame; the zero displacement $\Delta=0$ is none of the three and remains $0$ under every linear transition, so the classification statement is trivially chart-independent in that case. By step 1.1 the number $\eta_0(\Delta,\Delta)$ is unchanged under the transition, so the classification, and with it the sign of the interval, is chart-independent. For the future/past distinction, the displacement $q-p$ corresponds to the coordinate column $\Delta$, which is future causal exactly when the vector $E\Delta$ lies in $\operatorname{cl}(C^+)$; applying the linear map with matrix $\Lambda$ to a future causal coordinate vector gives a future causal coordinate vector by [L1], and applying the same statement to the inverse transition (whose linear part is $\Lambda^{-1}$) gives the converse, so future-relatedness is chart-independent. For the past case, $x\in\operatorname{cl}(C^-)$ holds exactly when $-x\in\operatorname{cl}(C^+)$, because $(-\operatorname{id})(C^+)=C^-$ by [L2] and $-\operatorname{id}$ is a bijective linear map, so it maps closures onto closures and carries the identity on the closed cones over to the closed cones; since $\Lambda(-\Delta)=-\Lambda\Delta$, the argument of the previous sentence applied to $-\Delta$ shows that past-relatedness is chart-independent as well. This proves (ii). [L1, L2, L4, L5, L6, algebra]

3.1 Let $\gamma(\lambda)=p+\lambda v$ be an ideal vacuum light ray with $v$ future null, so that in the chart $x$ its coordinate image is $x(p)+\lambda v_x$ with $v_x$ the coordinate column of $v$, a straight line of future null coordinate direction by [L9] and step 2.1. Under the transition the image is $x'(p)+\lambda\Lambda v_x$ by step 1.1: again a straight line, with direction $w:=\Lambda v_x$. The vector with coordinates $w$ is the image under the Lorentz map $L^{-1}$ of the future null vector $v$, hence is future null by [L2]; therefore the coordinate image is again a future null straight line, and applying the same argument to the inverse transition shows that the class of such lines is preserved in both directions. The coordinate speed statement is then the content of the light clause [L9] applied in the chart $x'$: for the future null direction $w$ one has $w^0=|w_{\mathrm{vec}}|>0$, so $|\Delta x|/\Delta t=c$ in every inertial chart. This proves (iii). [L2, L9, step 1.1, step 2.1, algebra]
