Adopt [[post-sr-massive-particle-dynamics]] (massive-particle momentum, the identification of measured quantities and isolated collision balance) and the SI conventions of [[def-sr-si-units-and-coordinate-conventions]]. Let $(A,V,\eta,C^+)$ be the affine Minkowski model, $c>0$, let $(o;e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3)$ be an inertial frame with stationary observer $n:=e_0$, spatial Euclidean structure $(S,\delta,|\cdot|)$ and inertial chart $x$ ([[def-inertial-frame-and-inertial-chart]], [[def-spatial-euclidean-structure-of-an-inertial-frame]]), and let a massive particle have constant mass $m>0$ and four-momentum $P=mU$ with $U$ future timelike, $\eta(U,U)=-c^2$. Let $y$ be a worldline of the particle whose inertial coordinate path is $t\mapsto(ct,r(t))$ and whose coordinate velocity $w(t)=r'(t)\in S$ of [[def-sr-newtonian-comparison-quantities]]\,(b) equals a fixed $w$ at the instant considered; then in this frame $P=m\gamma_w(c,w)$ with $\gamma_w=(1-|w|^2/c^2)^{-1/2}$ ([[lem-sr-four-momentum-in-inertial-frame]]\,(b), [[thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition]]\,(e)).

Fix $z_0\in[0,1)$ and suppose $z:=|w|^2/c^2\le z_0$; put $K(z_0):=\tfrac38(1-z_0)^{-5/2}$, and let $N_p(m,w)=mw$ and $N_K(m,w)=\tfrac12m|w|^2$ be the Newtonian comparison quantities of [[def-sr-newtonian-comparison-quantities]]. With $E_n(P)$, $q_n(P)$ and $T_n(P)$ the measured energy, spatial momentum and kinetic energy identified in clause (ii) of the adopted postulate, $m(P)$ the invariant mass of [[def-sr-observed-energy-momentum-and-kinetic-energy]] and $R_E,R_q$ the remainders of [[lem-sr-uniform-low-speed-expansion-of-observer-quantities]]:

(e) [Scope and uniformity] The constants $K(z_0)$ and $\tfrac12+K(z_0)z_0$ depend on $z_0$ alone, so the estimates hold uniformly over all masses $m>0$, all states, instants and inertial frames with $|w|^2\le z_0c^2$. The statement is a conditional correspondence between the model's adopted measured quantities and the comparison functionals of a named frame: it identifies no framework with another, asserts no convergence of trajectories, forces or interactions and no limit in which the constant $c$ varies, gives no bound uniform in $|w|<c$ (see [[rem-sr-newtonian-bridge-limits-and-failures]]) and makes no empirical claim.

**Given:** The affine Minkowski model with a fixed $c>0$ and the SI conventions $x^0=ct$; an inertial frame with stationary observer $n=e_0$, spatial structure $(S,\delta,|\cdot|)$ and chart $x$; a massive particle state $P=mU$ with constant $m>0$, $U$ future timelike and $\eta(U,U)=-c^2$, realized as the momentum of a $C^{1}$ worldline with future timelike tangent ([[def-sr-regular-causal-curve-and-worldline]]) whose coordinate velocity at the instant considered is a fixed $w\in S$; a bound $z_0\in[0,1)$ with $z=|w|^2/c^2\le z_0$; and $K(z_0)=\tfrac38(1-z_0)^{-5/2}$.

[L1] The adopted postulate: $P=mU$ with constant $m>0$ and $\eta(U,U)=-c^2$ (clause (i)); the model identifies the measured energy, spatial momentum, kinetic energy and rest energy of the particle with $E_n(P)$, $q_n(P)$, $T_n(P)=E_n(P)-mc^2$ and $mc^2$ (clause (ii)); units as in [[def-sr-si-units-and-coordinate-conventions]] ([[post-sr-massive-particle-dynamics]]).

[L2] The comparison functionals: for $w\in S$ of the named frame, $N_p(m,w)=mw$ and $N_K(m,w)=\tfrac12m|w|^2$; the coordinate velocity of a chart path $t\mapsto(ct,r(t))$ is $w(t)=r'(t)$ where it exists ([[def-sr-newtonian-comparison-quantities]]).

[L3] The SI conventions fix $x^0=ct$ in every inertial chart and the units metre, kilogram, second, joule and kilogram metre per second for the quantities used here ([[def-sr-si-units-and-coordinate-conventions]]).

[L4] The observer quantities: $E_n(P)=-c\eta(P,n)$, $q_n(P)=h(P)$, $m(P)=\sqrt{-\eta(P,P)}/c$, and $T_n(P)=E_n(P)-mc^2$ after the constant $m>0$ is fixed ([[def-sr-observed-energy-momentum-and-kinetic-energy]]).

[L5] The observer identities: for $P=mU$ with $m>0$ constant, $U$ future timelike with $\eta(U,U)=-c^2$, relative velocity $w$ and Lorentz factor $\gamma$ of [[thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition]]\,(d): $E_n(P)=mc^2\gamma$, $T_n(P)=mc^2(\gamma-1)$, $q_n(P)=m\gamma w$ and $m(P)=m$ ([[lem-sr-energy-momentum-observer-identities]]\,(b)).

[L6] The frame's stationary observer and the chart coordinate velocity: for $n=e_0$ the relative velocity of clause (d) is the chart coordinate velocity $w(t)=r'(t)$ of the worldline, with $|w|<c$ and $\gamma_w=(1-|w|^2/c^2)^{-1/2}$ ([[thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition]]\,(e)).

[L7] Frame components of the four-momentum: for $P=mU$ with $m>0$ constant the components in the frame are $P=m\gamma_w(c,w)$, that is $E_n(P)=m\gamma_wc^2$ and $q_n(P)=m\gamma_ww$ ([[lem-sr-four-momentum-in-inertial-frame]]\,(b)).

[L8] The uniform low-speed expansion of the observer quantities: with $\gamma=\gamma_w$ and $z=|w|^2/c^2\le z_0$, $E_n(P)=mc^2+\tfrac12m|w|^2+R_E$, $T_n(P)=\tfrac12m|w|^2+R_E$ and $q_n(P)=mw+R_q$ for $R_E=mc^2R(z)$, $R_q=m(\gamma_w-1)w$, with $|R_E|\le K(z_0)zm|w|^2=K(z_0)m|w|^4/c^2$, $\bigl|T_n(P)-\tfrac12m|w|^2\bigr|\le2K(z_0)z\,\tfrac12m|w|^2$ and $|R_q|\le(\tfrac12+K(z_0)z_0)z\,m|w|$; the constants depend only on $z_0$, and at $z=0$ the remainders vanish ([[lem-sr-uniform-low-speed-expansion-of-observer-quantities]]\,(a)-(c)).
[L9] The Taylor remainder: $\gamma_w=1+\tfrac z2+R(z)$ with $|R(z)|\le K(z_0)z^2$ for $0\le z\le z_0$ ([[lem-sr-uniform-low-speed-taylor-remainder]]\,(b)).

[L10] The model and frame structure: $(A,V,\eta,C^+)$ is the oriented time-oriented affine Minkowski model and the frame is an inertial frame with chart $x$ and spatial structure $(S,\delta,|\cdot|)$ ([[def-sr-affine-minkowski-model]], [[def-inertial-frame-and-inertial-chart]], [[def-spatial-euclidean-structure-of-an-inertial-frame]]).

Adopt [[post-sr-inertial-covariance]], [[post-sr-ideal-clocks-and-light]] and [[post-sr-ideal-plane-wave-model]], and the conventions of [[def-sr-si-units-and-coordinate-conventions]]. Let $x$ and $x'$ be inertial charts whose transition is $x'=B(\beta)x+b$ with $\beta\in\mathbb R^3$, $|\beta|<1$, $b\in\mathbb R^4$ and $B(\beta)$ the passive boost of [[def-lorentz-boost]]; write $\gamma:=(1-|\beta|^2)^{-1/2}$ and $\beta_{\mathrm{hat}}:=\beta/|\beta|$ for $\beta\ne0$, so that the frame $x'$ moves with velocity $v=c\beta$ relative to the frame $x$ in the direction $\beta_{\mathrm{hat}}$ (step 1.1 records this). Let the ideal wave of the model have phase $\theta$ with future null wave covector $k$ and frame-$x$ data $(\omega,s)$ in the sense of [[def-sr-null-wave-covector-and-observer-frequency]]: $\omega>0$, $s\in\mathbb R^3$ with $|s|=1$ and $k_a=(-\omega/c,(\omega/c)s_1,(\omega/c)s_2,(\omega/c)s_3)$ in $x$. Then, conditionally on the adopted model:

[A1] Adopted ideal plane-wave model: the level sets of $\theta$ are the wave fronts, the lines $p+\mathbb Rk^\sharp$ have constant phase, the rays are the future null straight lines $p+\mathbb R_{\ge0}k^\sharp$, and an ideal observer with four-velocity $U_o=cn$ reads the angular frequency $-ck(n)=-k(U_o)$ at the reception event ([[post-sr-ideal-plane-wave-model]]).

[A2] Adopted ideal light: ideal vacuum light rays are exactly the future null straight lines, with coordinate speed $c$ in every inertial chart, and real clocks and light are not claimed to be exactly ideal ([[post-sr-ideal-clocks-and-light]]).

[A3] Adopted inertial covariance: the inertial changes of description of the model are the affine maps with proper orthochronous Lorentz linear part, and covariance is asserted only for the specified model equations ([[post-sr-inertial-covariance]]).

[L1] With the SI conventions $x^0=ct$, the frame data $(\varpi,s)$ of $k$ in a frame and the wave data are related by $\varpi=\omega/c$, $|s|=1$, $\omega>0$, $k_a=(-\omega/c,(\omega/c)s_1,(\omega/c)s_2,(\omega/c)s_3)$, $\nu=\omega/(2\pi)$, $\lambda=c/\nu$; and an ideal observer with four-velocity $U_o=cn$ ($n$ future unit timelike) reads $\omega_n=-ck(n)=-k(U_o)>0$, which is minus the phase rate along the observer's worldline ([[def-sr-null-wave-covector-and-observer-frequency]], [[def-sr-si-units-and-coordinate-conventions]], [[lem-sr-null-covector-frame-data]], [[lem-sr-phase-rate-along-worldline]], [[def-sr-affine-phase-and-wave-covector]]).

[L2] Boost transformation of the frame data: for the chart pair of the Given, with $\varpi=\omega/c$ and $\beta\ne0$, the frame-$x'$ data $(\varpi',s')$ satisfies $\varpi'=\gamma(1-\beta\cdot s)\varpi$, $s'=\bigl[s+\frac{\gamma-1}{|\beta|^2}(\beta\cdot s)\beta-\gamma\beta\bigr]/\bigl[\gamma(1-\beta\cdot s)\bigr]$, $|s'|=1$ and $k'_a=(-\varpi',\varpi's')$; for $\beta=0$, $\varpi'=\varpi$, $s'=s$; in the axis case $\beta=be_1$, $s'_1=(s_1-b)/(1-bs_1)$, $s'_2=s_2/[\gamma(1-bs_1)]$, $s'_3=s_3/[\gamma(1-bs_1)]$; and $\beta\cdot s'=(\beta\cdot s-|\beta|^2)/(1-\beta\cdot s)$, with $\beta\cdot s'=0$ if and only if $\beta\cdot s=|\beta|^2$ ([[lem-sr-null-covector-boost-transformation]]).

[L3] $\gamma\ge1$ with equality exactly when $\beta=0$, $B(0)=\operatorname{id}$, and the matrix entries of $B(\beta)$ and $B(-\beta)$ are as displayed in [[def-lorentz-boost]]; the transition $x'=B(\beta)x+b$ of inertial charts has proper orthochronous linear part ([[lem-inertial-chart-transitions-are-affine-lorentz]]), and $B(-\beta)=B(\beta)^{-1}$ ([[lem-sr-null-covector-boost-transformation]], clause (v)).

[L4] In an inertial frame the basis vectors satisfy $\eta(e_a,e_b)=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$ with $e_0$ future, so $e_0$ and $e'_0$ are future unit timelike; the four-velocity of an observer at rest in a frame is $c$ times its first basis vector, and a point observer is a future unit timelike vector $n$ ([[def-inertial-frame-and-inertial-chart]], [[def-sr-four-velocity-and-four-acceleration]]).

[L5] Frame and component relations between the charts: the transition $x'=\Lambda x+b$ has linear part $\Lambda=B(\beta)$, the new frame's basis vectors satisfy $e'_a=\sum_b(\Lambda^{-1})^b{}_ae_b$, and the components of a covector satisfy $k'_a=(\Lambda^{-1})^b{}_ak_b$ with $\Lambda^{-1}=B(-\beta)$; in the chart of any inertial frame an affine phase with wave covector $k$ has the form $\theta(p)=k_ax^a(p)+\theta(o)$ ([[lem-inertial-chart-transitions-are-affine-lorentz]], [[lem-sr-null-covector-boost-transformation]], [[def-lorentz-boost]], [[def-sr-affine-phase-and-wave-covector]]).

[L6] Relative velocity and coordinate form: for future unit timelike $n,u$, with $\gamma_{rel}:=-\eta(n,u)$ and $h(v):=v+\eta(n,v)n$, the vector $w:=ch(u)/\gamma_{rel}$ lies in $n^\perp$ and is the velocity of the worldline with four-velocity $cu$ relative to the observer $n$; a worldline with coordinate velocity $w$ in an inertial chart, $|w|<c$, has four-velocity $U=\gamma_w(c,w_{\mathrm{vec}})$ with $\gamma_w=(1-|w|^2/c^2)^{-1/2}$, so $n=U/c=\gamma_w(1,w/c)$ is future unit timelike ([[thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition]], clauses (a), (c), (d), (e)).

[L7] The spatial three-space of an inertial frame carries the positive-definite form $\delta$, and the vectors $\beta,s,w$ of the statement are vectors of that space with Euclidean norms and scalar products; in particular $s'\cdot\beta_{\mathrm{hat}}=(\beta\cdot s')/|\beta|$ for $\beta\ne0$ ([[def-spatial-euclidean-structure-of-an-inertial-frame]]). The factor $1-\beta\cdot s$ is positive because [L2] exhibits $\varpi'=\gamma(1-\beta\cdot s)\varpi$ with $\varpi,\varpi',\gamma>0$.

Adopt the ideal-clock and ideal-light assumptions of [[post-sr-ideal-clocks-and-light]] and the inertial-covariance assumption of [[post-sr-inertial-covariance]], and the SI coordinate conventions of [[def-sr-si-units-and-coordinate-conventions]]. Let the inertial frames and charts $x$, $x'$ related by a boost of parameter $v$ along the common first spatial direction be as in [[lem-sr-boost-time-length-and-velocity-formulas]], with $\gamma=(1-v^2/c^2)^{-1/2}$. Then, as statements about the ideal model and not about any actual apparatus:

**(i) Moving clocks run slow.** An ideal clock carried along the worldline $y(\lambda)=x^{-1}\bigl(\lambda,\tfrac{v}{c}\lambda+a_1,a_2,a_3\bigr)$ of clause (i) of the lemma reads between parameter values $\lambda_0<\lambda_1$ the time $(\lambda_1-\lambda_0)/(c\gamma)$, and since the coordinate time of $x$ along $y$ is $t=\lambda/c$, this is $(t_1-t_0)/\gamma$; equivalently, between two events of the clock's history the coordinate time elapsed in $x$ is $\Delta t=\gamma\,\Delta\tau$, where $\Delta\tau$ is the clock's reading ([[def-sr-proper-time]], [[def-sr-regular-causal-curve-and-worldline]]). Symmetrically, with $x$ and $x'$ interchanged, a clock at rest in $x$ runs slow by the same factor in the frame $x'$.

**(ii) Length contraction.** For a rod at rest in the frame $x'$ of rest length $L_0>0$, with endpoints carried along the worldlines $y_a$, $y_b$ of clause (ii) of the lemma, the length assigned to it by the frame $x$ on a simultaneity slice of $x$ in the sense of [[def-sr-simultaneity-slice-and-rest-distance]] is $L_0/\gamma$; symmetrically, a rod at rest in $x$ has length $L_0/\gamma$ as measured by $x'$. Measured length here is defined by the stated protocol — the rest distance between the two endpoint events at equal time in the measuring frame — and it is not the optical appearance of a moving rod; no claim is made about a rod whose state of motion changes.

**(iii) Relativity of simultaneity.** If two events $p,q$ satisfy $x^0(q)-x^0(p)=0$ and $x^1(q)-x^1(p)=L$, with vanishing transverse coordinate difference, then $x'^0(q)-x'^0(p)=-\gamma\tfrac{v}{c}L$, which is nonzero whenever $vL\ne0$; hence simultaneity in $x$ is not simultaneity in $x'$ and is not an observer-independent relation. Each inertial frame's simultaneity is exactly the simultaneity relation of its time axis in the sense of [[def-sr-simultaneity-slice-and-rest-distance]], operationally reproduced by its radar protocol as established in [[pthm-sr-radar-synchronization-of-inertial-observers]].

so relative velocities are not simply added; moreover $|w'|<c$ whenever $|w|<c$. Equivalently, $w'$ is the velocity of the worldline relative to the observer with four-velocity direction $e'_0$ in the sense of clause (d) of [[thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition]] ([[def-sr-four-velocity-and-four-acceleration]]).

**Given:** The adopted ideal-clock/ideal-light and inertial-covariance postulates and the SI conventions ([[post-sr-ideal-clocks-and-light]], [[post-sr-inertial-covariance]], [[def-sr-si-units-and-coordinate-conventions]]), two inertial frames with charts $x$, $x'$ related by the boost of parameter $v$, $|v|<c$, with $\gamma=(1-v^2/c^2)^{-1/2}$, and the data of clauses (i)-(iv) of the Statement ([[def-inertial-frame-and-inertial-chart]]).

[F1] Boost formulas ([[lem-sr-boost-time-length-and-velocity-formulas]]): (i) the worldline $y(\lambda)=x^{-1}(\lambda,\tfrac{v}{c}\lambda+a_1,a_2,a_3)$ is future timelike and its proper time between $\lambda_0<\lambda_1$ is $(\lambda_1-\lambda_0)/(c\gamma)$; (ii) for the worldlines $y_a,y_b$ at rest in $x'$ with $x'$-separation $L_0$, the $x'$-separation at equal $x'$-times is $L_0$ while the $x$-separation at equal $x$-times is $L_0/\gamma$, and symmetrically with the frames interchanged; (iii) $x^0(q)-x^0(p)=0$, $x^1(q)-x^1(p)=L$ imply $x'^0(q)-x'^0(p)=-\gamma\tfrac{v}{c}L$; (iv) for a $C^1$ future timelike worldline with subluminal coordinate velocity $w$ in $x$, the coordinate velocity in $x'$ is $w'_1=(w_1-v)/(1-vw_1/c^2)$, $w'_\perp=w_\perp/\bigl(\gamma(1-vw_1/c^2)\bigr)$, and $|w'|<c$ when $|w|<c$.

[F2] Ideal clocks read proper time: an ideal clock carried along a $C^1$ future timelike curve reads between parameters $a<b$ the value $\sigma(b)-\sigma(a)=c^{-1}\int_a^b\sqrt{-\eta(x',x')}\,ds$, with no acceleration-dependent term ([[post-sr-ideal-clocks-and-light]] clause (i), [[def-sr-proper-time]]).

[F3] Radar theorem: for an inertial observer with chart $x$ and an event $q$ with nonzero spatial coordinates, the radar time is $x^0(q)/c$ and the radar distance is the chart's rest-frame distance $|r|$, up to the fixed additive constant of the observer's proper-time origin ([[pthm-sr-radar-synchronization-of-inertial-observers]], [[def-sr-simultaneity-slice-and-rest-distance]]).

(iii) **Radar time and distance to a coaxial congruence reflector.** Fix $\rho_m > 0$ with $\rho_m \ne \rho_0$ and let $R_m$ be the congruence worldline $\rho = \rho_m$, $y = y_0$, $z = z_0$ (a second uniformly accelerated observer, coaxial with $O$, with proper acceleration $c^2/\rho_m$). Let $e_-$ be the event of $O$ at parameter $\theta_e$ (so $\tau(e_-) = \rho_0 \theta_e/c$ up to the base point of $\tau$), let $q_m$ be the event of $R_m$ lying on the future null straight line from $e_-$ in the plane $y = y_0$, $z = z_0$, and let $e_+$ be the event of $O$ lying on the future null straight line from $q_m$; the reflection at $q_m$ is idealized as instantaneous and as leaving $R_m$'s motion unchanged, as in [[def-sr-operational-radar-protocol]]. Then $e_-, q_m, e_+$ exist uniquely, the Rindler time of $q_m$ is $\theta_m = \theta_e + |\log(\rho_m/\rho_0)|$, the return event satisfies $\theta(e_+) = \theta_e + 2|\log(\rho_m/\rho_0)|$ and $(\theta_e + \theta(e_+))/2 = \theta_m$, so the round trip lasts $2|\log(\rho_m/\rho_0)|$ in Rindler time and $(2\rho_0/c)|\log(\rho_m/\rho_0)|$ in $O$'s proper time. The radar protocol therefore assigns to $q_m$ the radar time $\tau_{\mathrm{rad}}(q_m) = (\rho_0/c) \theta_m$ plus the base constant of $\tau$ and the radar distance $\rho_{\mathrm{rad}}(q_m) = \rho_0 |\log(\rho_m/\rho_0)|$; within this coaxial family the radar-time level sets are exactly the Rindler simultaneity slices $\theta = \mathrm{const}$, i.e. the rest slices of the congruence ([[def-sr-simultaneity-slice-and-rest-distance]]). The radar distance is not the rest distance: in the slice $\theta = \theta_m$ the two worldlines are at rest distance $|\rho_m - \rho_0|$, whereas for $\rho_m = 2\rho_0$ the radar distance is $\rho_0 \log 2 < \rho_0$, because $\log$ is strictly increasing and $e > 2$ implies $\log 2 < \log e = 1$ ([[cor-two-less-than-e-less-than-three]], [[thm-natural-logarithm-laws]]). For every distinct positive reflector radius the notions differ: with $r = \rho_m/\rho_0$, one has $\log r < r - 1$ when $r > 1$ and $-\log r > 1 - r$ when $0 < r < 1$. The two distance formulas agree only at $r = 1$, where both have the continuous degenerate value zero. The coincident case is not a nonzero emission-reflection-reception triple of the protocol, whose distinct-reflector hypothesis remains in force. As $\rho_m \to 0^+$ the round-trip proper time and the radar distance grow without bound while the reflector's proper acceleration $c^2/\rho_m$ diverges; as $\rho_m \to +\infty$ the round-trip proper time and the radar distance also grow without bound while the reflector's proper acceleration tends to $0$.

[L1] A linear Lorentz map is a linear $L$ with $\eta(Lv,Lw)=\eta(v,w)$ for all $v,w$; it is proper when $\det L=+1$ and orthochronous when $L(C^+)=C^+$; $GL(V)$ is the group of invertible linear maps ([[def-lorentz-map-and-lorentz-group]]).

[L2] Every linear Lorentz map is a linear isomorphism, satisfies $\det L=\pm1$, preserves $\eta(v,v)$ and the causal character of every nonzero vector, and maps $C^+$ onto one of the two components $C^+,C^-$ of the timelike set; $L(C^+)=C^+$ holds if and only if $L(C^+)\subseteq C^+$; $SO(V,\eta)=\{L:\det L=1\}$, $O^{\uparrow}(V,\eta)=\{L:L(C^+)=C^+\}$ and $SO^+(V,\eta)=SO(V,\eta)\cap O^{\uparrow}(V,\eta)$ are subgroups of $O(V,\eta)$, which is a subgroup of $GL(V)$; if $L$ is proper then $\epsilon(Lv_0,\dots,Lv_3)=\epsilon(v_0,\dots,v_3)$ and if $\det L=-1$ the two sides differ by the sign $-1$ ([[lem-lorentz-map-preserves-metric-and-causal-structure]], [[def-oriented-minkowski-volume-form]]).

[L3] For every $|\boldsymbol\beta|<1$ the passive boost $B(\boldsymbol\beta)$ is a proper orthochronous Lorentz map with $B(\boldsymbol\beta)^{-1}=B(-\boldsymbol\beta)$; the map $\boldsymbol\beta\mapsto B(\boldsymbol\beta)$ is injective and $B(\mathbf 0)=\operatorname{id}_V$ ([[lem-boost-is-proper-orthochronous-with-inverse]], [[def-lorentz-boost]]).

[L4] For every unit spatial vector $e$ and all $\beta_1,\beta_2\in(-1,1)$, $B(\beta_1e)B(\beta_2e)=B\bigl(\frac{\beta_1+\beta_2}{1+\beta_1\beta_2}e\bigr)$ with $\bigl|\frac{\beta_1+\beta_2}{1+\beta_1\beta_2}\bigr|<1$, and the two collinear boosts commute ([[lem-collinear-boost-composition-and-velocity-addition]]).

[L5] The map $r\mapsto\tanh(r)$ is a strictly increasing bijection of $\mathbb R$ onto $(-1,1)$, and for every unit spatial vector $e$ and all $r,s\in\mathbb R$ one has $B(\tanh(r)e)B(\tanh(s)e)=B(\tanh(r+s)e)$ ([[lem-rapidity-parametrization-of-collinear-boosts]]).

[L6] For a proper orthochronous Lorentz map $L$ with $u:=Le_0$ and coordinates $(u^0,u_{\mathrm{vec}})$, the parameter $\boldsymbol\beta:=u_{\mathrm{vec}}/u^0$ satisfies $|\boldsymbol\beta|<1$, and $L=B(-\boldsymbol\beta)\widehat R$ with $\widehat R:=B(\boldsymbol\beta)L$ the extension $\operatorname{diag}(1,R)$ of a spatial rotation of the frame; this factorization is unique among parameters in the open unit ball and spatial rotations; conversely every such $B(-\boldsymbol\beta)\widehat R$ is proper orthochronous; and $L$ is a passive boost if and only if $\widehat R=\operatorname{id}_V$ ([[lem-boost-rotation-factorization]]).

Let $(A,V,\eta,C^+)$ be the oriented time-oriented affine Minkowski space ([[def-sr-affine-minkowski-model]]), let $n$ be a smooth future unit timelike field on a nonempty open subset $\Omega\subseteq A$ ([[def-sr-chart-tetrad-and-congruence-distinction]]), with acceleration $a=\nabla_nn$, rest metric $h$, expansion $\theta$ and vorticity $\omega$ ([[def-sr-observer-congruence-and-kinematics]]), and assume that $n$ is Born rigid, $\theta=0$; write $a^\flat:=\eta(a,\cdot)$.

**(ii) Rotational case.** Let $U\subseteq\Omega$ be a flow box of $n$ with adapted coordinates $(s,y^1,y^2,y^3)$ in which $n=\partial_s$ ([[thm-sr-local-congruence-adapted-charts-and-frobenius]]), and suppose that $\omega$ is nowhere zero on $U$. Then the vorticity and the acceleration are **basic** on $U$: they are horizontal and their components in the adapted coframe do not depend on $s$, equivalently $\mathcal L_n\omega=0$ and $\mathcal L_na^\flat=0$. Moreover $da^\flat=0$ on $U$, and for every primitive $F$ of the closed one-form $a^\flat$ on the star-shaped box $U$ ([[thm-poincare-lemma-for-differential-forms-on-star-shaped-domains]]) the field $K:=e^Fn$ is a timelike Killing field, $\nabla_aK_b+\nabla_bK_a=0$, equivalently $\mathcal L_K\eta=0$. If $U$ is connected and simply connected and $\omega$ is nowhere zero, then a single positive smooth function $f$ on $U$ satisfies $\mathcal L_{fn}\eta=0$ ([[lem-sr-closed-one-form-primitive-on-simply-connected-open-sets]]). Conversely, every future timelike Killing field on a connected open set, normalized as $n=K/\sqrt{-\eta(K,K)}$, is Born rigid, and its vorticity is either nowhere zero or identically zero on that set; hence its flow is rotational, in the sense of case (ii), exactly when its vorticity is nowhere zero.

**Given:** The oriented time-oriented affine Minkowski space $(A,V,\eta,C^+)$ with tangent spaces identified with $V$, a smooth future unit timelike field $n$ on a nonempty open subset $\Omega\subseteq A$ with $\theta=0$, the objects $h,a,\theta,\omega$ of [[def-sr-observer-congruence-and-kinematics]], the flat covariant derivative $\nabla$ of [[def-flat-covariant-derivative-on-affine-minkowski-space]], and, in clauses (ii) and (iii), the flow boxes and curves described in the Statement ([[def-sr-affine-minkowski-model]], [[def-sr-chart-tetrad-and-congruence-distinction]]).

[F1] In an inertial chart of the model, $\eta(u,v)=-u^0v^0+u^1v^1+u^2v^2+u^3v^3$, the tangent space at each event is canonically identified with $V$, and the flat covariant derivative acts on components by ordinary coordinate derivatives: $(

[F2] Kinematics of the congruence: $\nabla_an_b=-n_aa_b+\theta_{ab}+\omega_{ab}$, with $a_b=\eta_{bc}a^c$ and $a=\nabla_nn$; $\theta$ is symmetric and $\omega$ antisymmetric; both are horizontal, $\theta_{ab}n^b=\omega_{ab}n^b=n^a\theta_{ab}=n^a\omega_{ab}=0$; $h=\eta+n^\flat\otimes n^\flat$ satisfies $h(v,w)=\eta(h(v),h(w))$ with $h(v)=v+\eta(n,v)n$, its radical is spanned by $n$ and its restriction to $n^\perp$ is positive definite; Born rigidity is $\mathcal L_nh=0$, equivalently $\theta=0$; and $a^\flat(n)=0$ ([[def-sr-observer-congruence-and-kinematics]], [[thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition]] clause (c), [[def-lorentz-orthogonality-and-orthogonal-complement]]).

[F3] Flow box and adapted charts: a smooth nowhere-zero vector field is locally $\partial/\partial u^0$ in suitable coordinates, and every observer congruence admits local adapted charts; in particular $n=\partial_s$ in coordinates $(s,y^1,y^2,y^3)$ on a flow box $U$, and the integral curves of $n$ are its $s$-lines ([[thm-flow-box-theorem]], [[thm-sr-local-congruence-adapted-charts-and-frobenius]], [[def-integral-curve-of-a-vector-field]]).

[F4] Connection one-forms and curvature two-forms: for a local frame $e_A$ with dual coframe $\theta^A$, the connection matrix $\gamma^A{}_B$ is defined by $\nabla_Xe_B=\gamma^A{}_B(X)e_A$, and the curvature two-forms satisfy $\Omega^A{}_B=d\gamma^A{}_B+\gamma^A{}_C\wedge\gamma^C{}_B$ with $R(X,Y)e_B=\Omega^A{}_B(X,Y)e_A$ ([[def-connection-one-form-in-a-local-frame]], [[thm-curvature-two-form-structure-equation]]). For the flat connection of [F1], $\Omega^A{}_B=0$ ([[def-flat-covariant-derivative-on-affine-minkowski-space]], clause (c)).

[F7] Primitives: every closed smooth one-form on a star-shaped open domain has a smooth primitive, and every closed $C^1$ one-form on a nonempty path-connected simply connected open subset of $A$ has a $C^2$ primitive; a form is closed when $d\alpha=0$ ([[thm-poincare-lemma-for-differential-forms-on-star-shaped-domains]], [[lem-sr-closed-one-form-primitive-on-simply-connected-open-sets]], [[def-closed-and-exact-differential-forms]]).

[F11] Curves and integral curves: through every point of $\Omega$ there is a unique maximal integral curve of $n$, and a $C^1$ curve with $\gamma'=n\circ\gamma$ is smooth because $n$ is smooth and $s\mapsto n(\gamma(s))$ is then $C^1$, so $\gamma'$ is $C^1$ and $\gamma$ is $C^2$; iterating gives smoothness ([[def-integral-curve-of-a-vector-field]], [[thm-unique-maximal-integral-curve-through-each-point]], [[thm-chain-rule]], [[def-derivative]]). Every such maximal curve with $n$ future unit is a future timelike worldline ([[def-sr-regular-causal-curve-and-worldline]], [[def-causal-classification-of-lorentz-vectors]], [[def-time-orientation-and-future-causal-sets]]).

[F13] Frobenius criterion for rest distributions: on an open set the rest distribution $\ker n^\flat$ is integrable if and only if $\omega=0$ there, if and only if $n^\flat\wedge d(n^\flat)=0$; when it is integrable, its integral hypersurfaces are the pointwise rest slices $n^\perp$ ([[thm-sr-local-congruence-adapted-charts-and-frobenius]], clause (iii)).

Let $x$ be an inertial chart of the affine Minkowski model with coordinates $(x^0,x^1,x^2,x^3)$, let $B:=\prod_{a=0}^{3}[c_a,d_a]$ with $c_a<d_a$ be a closed axis-parallel box, and let $T$ be a $C^1$ symmetric type-$(2,0)$ tensor field on an open neighbourhood of $B$; put $f^b:=\partial_aT^{ab}$ (continuous on $B$) as in [[def-sr-stress-energy-tensor-and-force-density]]. (a) (Box identity.) For each $b$, with $F_a^+:=\{x\in B:x^a=d_a\}$, $F_a^-:=\{x\in B:x^a=c_a\}$ and each face integral the Riemann integral over the remaining three coordinates, $$\int_B f^b\,d^4x=\sum_{a=0}^{3}\Big(\int_{F_a^+}T^{ab}\,d^3x-\int_{F_a^-}T^{ab}\,d^3x\Big).$$ (b) (Slice balance.) Write $K:=\prod_{i=1}^{3}[c_i,d_i]$ and, for $s\in[c_0,d_0]$, $Q^b(s):=\int_K T^{0b}(s,x)\,d^3x$; this is finite and continuous in $s$. For $c_0\le s_1<s_2\le d_0$, $$Q^b(s_2)-Q^b(s_1)=\int_{[s_1,s_2]\times K} f^b\,d^4x-\sum_{i=1}^{3}\Big(\int_{[s_1,s_2]\times K_i^+}T^{ib}\,d^3x-\int_{[s_1,s_2]\times K_i^-}T^{ib}\,d^3x\Big),$$ where $K_i^\pm$ are the two faces $x^i=d_i$, $x^i=c_i$ of $K$. (c) (Finite-flux conservation.) If $f=0$ on $[s_1,s_2]\times K$ and $T^{ib}=0$ on the side faces $[s_1,s_2]\times K_i^\pm$ for $i=1,2,3$, then $Q^b(s_1)=Q^b(s_2)$ for every $b$. The theorem concerns finite axis-parallel boxes in one inertial chart and is proved by the fundamental theorem of calculus. It does not assert a flux identity for arbitrary regions or hypersurfaces, does not assert that $Q^b$ transforms as a four-vector under a change of inertial chart, and asserts no conservation without the stated side-flux hypothesis; no noncompact or limiting statement is made. No choice principle is used.

**Given:** The affine Minkowski model with an inertial chart $x$ ([[def-sr-affine-minkowski-model]], [[def-inertial-frame-and-inertial-chart]]), a closed nondegenerate axis-parallel box $B=\prod_{a=0}^3[c_a,d_a]$, and a $C^1$ symmetric type-$(2,0)$ field $T$ on an open neighbourhood $U\supseteq B$ ([[def-ck-tensor-field-on-minkowski-space]]); the components $T^{ab}$ are $C^1$ functions on $U$ and $f^b=\partial_aT^{ab}$ with $\partial_a$ the coordinate partial derivatives. For a face $F_a^\pm$ of a box, its face integral is the Riemann integral of the restricted continuous function over the product of the remaining three coordinate intervals.

[L1] The transition of two inertial charts is affine with linear part $\Lambda=M^{-1}$, the matrix of the proper orthochronous linear Lorentz map $L$ with $Le_a=e'_a$; the linear parts of transitions are exactly the proper orthochronous Lorentz matrices and their inverses ([[lem-inertial-chart-transitions-are-affine-lorentz]]).

[L2] A linear Lorentz map is a linear isomorphism preserving $\eta$; its matrix in an orthonormal basis satisfies the metric condition; it is proper when its determinant is $+1$ and orthochronous when it maps $C^+$ onto $C^+$; the affine Lorentz maps form a group ([[def-lorentz-map-and-lorentz-group]], [[lem-lorentz-map-preserves-metric-and-causal-structure]]).

[L3] A $\mathcal C^k$ type-$(r,s)$ tensor field on $\Omega$ assigns to $p\in\Omega$ a multilinear $T(p):(V^*)^r\times V^s\to\mathbb R$, with components $T^{a_1\dots a_r}{}_{b_1\dots b_s}(p)=T(p)(e^{*a_1},\dots,e_{b_1},\dots)$ in a frame, and regularity is chart-independent ([[def-ck-tensor-field-on-minkowski-space]], [[def-type-r-s-tensor-on-a-finite-dimensional-vector-space]]).

[L6] An alternating $k$-linear map is a $k$-linear map vanishing whenever two arguments coincide ([[def-alternating-k-linear-map]]); the oriented volume form of the model is $\epsilon(v_0,\dots,v_3)=\det([v_j^a])$ in an inertial frame, an alternating $4$-linear form with $\epsilon_{0123}=+1$ ([[def-oriented-minkowski-volume-form]]).

[L7] For a proper linear Lorentz map $L$ the oriented volume form satisfies $\epsilon(Lv_0,\dots,Lv_3)=\epsilon(v_0,\dots,v_3)$, and for $\det L=-1$ the two sides differ by the sign $-1$ ([[lem-lorentz-map-preserves-metric-and-causal-structure]]).

[L8] At $\boldsymbol\beta=\mathbf0$ the boost is the identity; the quotient expressions below are used only for nonzero $\boldsymbol\beta$, with their spatial correction interpreted as zero at $\boldsymbol\beta=\mathbf0$. The passive boost with parameter $\boldsymbol\beta$ has the coordinate action and matrix displayed in [[def-lorentz-boost]], with inverse $B(-\boldsymbol\beta)$, and $\gamma=(1-|\boldsymbol\beta|^2)^{-1/2}$ ([[lem-boost-is-proper-orthochronous-with-inverse]]).

[L9] In an inertial chart, $x(p)=E^{-1}(p-o)$ with $E$ the coordinate isomorphism and $\eta(e_a,e_b)=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)_{ab}$ ([[def-inertial-frame-and-inertial-chart]]). For the conditional coordinate-velocity interpretation in clause (vii), fix a real constant $c>0$ and define the reparametrized coordinate $t:=x^0/c$. This is a mathematical rescaling; no SI unit or physical-clock identification is assumed.

relevant_body_uses.text: Let $x:I\to A$ be a $C^2$ future timelike worldline with four-velocity $U=dx/d\tau$ and four-acceleration $A=dU/d\tau$ ([[def-sr-four-velocity-and-four-acceleration]], [[def-sr-regular-causal-curve-and-worldline]]), so that $\eta(U,U)=-c^2$ and $\eta(U,A)=0$ ([[thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition]]), write $s$ for its given parameter and $\tau$ for its proper-time function, with $\tau'(s)>0$, and let $X:I\to V$ be a $C^1$ field along $x$ ([[def-vector-field-and-section-along-a-smooth-curve]]).

where $X'$ denotes differentiation with respect to $s$ and $dX/d\tau:=X'/\tau'$. Here $\tau'=c^{-1}\sqrt{-\eta(x',x')}>0$ by [[def-sr-four-velocity-and-four-acceleration]]. The derivative $X'$ is the ordinary $V$-valued derivative of $X$, which is the covariant derivative of $X$ along $x$ in the flat model ([[def-flat-covariant-derivative-on-affine-minkowski-space]], clause (d)). The field $X$ is **Fermi–Walker transported along $x$** when $D_{\mathrm{FW}}X/d\tau=0$, that is, when

- **Well-definedness.** For a $C^2$ worldline the fields $U$ and $A$ are continuous and $U$ is nowhere zero, so the coefficients $\tau'\eta(A,\cdot)/c^2$ and $\tau'\eta(U,\cdot)/c^2$ of the transport equation are continuous functions along $x$; the equation $X'=\tau'c^{-2}\bigl(\eta(A,X)U-\eta(U,X)A\bigr)$ is therefore a first-order linear differential equation for the $V$-valued field $X$ ([[def-vector-field-and-section-along-a-smooth-curve]], [[def-flat-covariant-derivative-on-affine-minkowski-space]], clause (d)). This definition fixes the rule and does not assert that solutions exist; existence, uniqueness and the preservation of the tetrad conditions are the content of the following lemma.

- **Clause (b) is a computation, not a definition.** The two identities used, $\eta(U,U)=-c^2$ and $\eta(U,A)=0$, are clauses (a) and (b) of [[thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition]]; the cancellation displayed in (b) is then immediate from the bilinearity of $\eta$. The definition deliberately introduces no norm or orthogonality claim of its own.

- **Fermi–Walker transport of tensors along a worldline.** The same rule may be applied to any $C^1$ tensor field along $x$ by subtracting the covariant derivatives of all tensor arguments ([[def-ck-tensor-field-on-minkowski-space]]); in this framework only the vector case with the fields $E_a$ and the four-velocity is used, and no additional structure (connection coefficients, Christoffel symbols, curvature) is needed because the model's covariant derivative along a curve is the ordinary $V$-valued derivative.

Let $n$ be an observer congruence on a nonempty open subset $\Omega\subseteq A$ ([[def-sr-chart-tetrad-and-congruence-distinction]]), let $\nabla$ be the flat covariant derivative of the affine model ([[def-flat-covariant-derivative-on-affine-minkowski-space]]), and write $n_b:=\eta_{bc}n^c$ for the associated covector field ([[def-ck-tensor-field-on-minkowski-space]]).

**(a) Rest metric and projection.** Define $h(v,w):=\eta(v,w)+\eta(n,v)\eta(n,w)$ for vectors at the same point, so that $h=\eta+n^\flat\otimes n^\flat$ in components. Then $h(v,w)=\eta(h(v),h(w))$ for the orthogonal projection $h(v):=v+\eta(n,v)n$ of [[thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition]] clause (c). At every point $h$ is symmetric with radical spanned by $n(p)$, and its restriction to $n(p)^\perp$ is positive definite ([[def-lorentz-orthogonality-and-orthogonal-complement]]).

**(b) Acceleration.** The **acceleration** of the congruence is $a:=\nabla_nn$. Then $\eta(n,a)=0$ pointwise, because $2\eta(n,\nabla_nn)=n\bigl(\eta(n,n)\bigr)=0$; consequently $a(p)$ is spacelike or zero by the causal classification ([[def-causal-classification-of-lorentz-vectors]]). In the model's physical interpretation the four-acceleration of the congruence observers is $c^2a$ and its magnitude is $c^2\sqrt{\eta(a,a)}$; the numerical units belong to the model's SI conventions and are not part of the affine geometry ([[def-sr-four-velocity-and-four-acceleration]]).

- **Clause (a) is an expansion identity.** Using $\eta(n,n)=-1$ and bilinearity, $\eta(h(v),h(w))=\eta(v,w)+2\eta(n,v)\eta(n,w)+\eta(n,v)\eta(n,w)\eta(n,n)=\eta(v,w)+\eta(n,v)\eta(n,w)=h(v,w)$; the radical and positive-definiteness statements are clause (c) of [[thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition]] together with [[def-lorentz-orthogonality-and-orthogonal-complement]].

- **Clause (b) computes the acceleration as a derivative along $n$.** With metric compatibility of $
abla$ ([[def-flat-covariant-derivative-on-affine-minkowski-space]] clause (c)) one has $n igl(\eta(n,n) igr)=
abla_n igl(\eta(n,n) igr)=2\eta(n,
abla_nn)$, and $\eta(n,n)=-1$ has zero derivative; hence $\eta(n,a)=0$, so $a$ is spacelike wherever it is nonzero. The identification of the observers' four-acceleration with $c^2a$ is the chain rule: parametrize an observer by the congruence parameter $s$, so that its tangent is $x'(s)=n(x(s))$ ([[def-sr-chart-tetrad-and-congruence-distinction]] clause (c)); its four-velocity is $U=x'/	au'=cn$ because $\eta(x',x')=-1$ forces $	au'=1/c$ ([[def-sr-four-velocity-and-four-acceleration]]), and differentiating the components of $U$ along the curve in an inertial chart gives $U'(s)=c\,\partial_bn^a(x(s))x'^b(s)=c\,(
abla_nn)^a(x(s))$, so the four-acceleration $A=U'/	au'=c^2a$ ([[thm-chain-rule]]).

Let $k\ne0$ be a null covector, $\eta^{ab}k_ak_b=0$, with $k^\sharp$ future, let $f:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$ be smooth, $\theta_0\in\mathbb R$, and let $\varphi(x):=f(k_ax^a+\theta_0)$ in an inertial chart; take $V\equiv0$ and $K>0$. Then $\varphi$ solves the massless scalar-field equation of [[lem-sr-scalar-field-euler-lagrange]], and its Hilbert stress-energy tensor is the conserved tensor $$T^{ab}=Kf'(k_ax^a+\theta_0)^2\,k^ak^b,$$ a nonnegative multiple of the rank-one future-null tensor $k^\sharp\otimes k^\sharp$ wherever $f'\ne0$ and the zero tensor wherever $f'=0$.

**Given:** The affine Minkowski model with inertial chart $x$, constant $\eta_{ab}=\eta^{ab}=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$ ([[def-sr-affine-minkowski-model]], [[def-lorentz-form-and-inertia]]), coordinate partials $\partial_a$ ([[def-directional-and-partial-derivatives]]); a nonzero null covector $k$ with $k^\sharp$ future ($k^ak_a=0$, $k^a=\eta^{ab}k_b\ne0$, $k^0>0$) ([[def-causal-classification-of-lorentz-vectors]], [[def-time-orientation-and-future-causal-sets]]); smooth $f$, $\theta:=k_ax^a+\theta_0$; $V\equiv0$, $K>0$; $\varphi=f\circ\theta$, a smooth scalar field ([[def-ck-tensor-field-on-minkowski-space]]).

[F2] Scalar-field equation and Hilbert tensor: the field equation of the model with potential $V$ is $\Box\varphi=V'(\varphi)$, and the Hilbert tensor of the density with this $V$ is $T^{ab}=K[\partial^a\varphi\partial^b\varphi-\eta^{ab}(\tfrac12\partial_d\varphi\partial^d\varphi+V(\varphi))]$. **(a) [Dimensional exclusion of $E=\varepsilon_0D$]** In the SI conventions of [[def-em-si-conventions]]: the electric constant $\varepsilon_0=(\mu_0c^2)^{-1}$ carries $\mathrm F\,\mathrm m^{-1}=\mathrm C^2\mathrm s^2\,\mathrm{kg}^{-1}\mathrm m^{-3}$, the displacement $D$ of [[def-em-polarization-magnetization]] carries $\mathrm C\,\mathrm m^{-2}$, and the electric field $E$ of [[def-em-fields]] carries $\mathrm V\,\mathrm m^{-1}=\mathrm{kg}\,\mathrm m\,\mathrm s^{-2}\mathrm C^{-1}$. The product $\varepsilon_0D$ therefore carries $\mathrm F\,\mathrm C\,\mathrm m^{-3}=\mathrm C^3\mathrm s^2\,\mathrm{kg}^{-1}\mathrm m^{-5}$, which is not the dimension of $E$: the proposed identification $E=\varepsilon_0D$ fails dimensionally in SI and cannot be a field relation of the framework.

**(b) [Units do not determine the law]** Solving the definition $D=\varepsilon_0E+P$ of [[def-em-polarization-magnetization]] gives $E=(D-P)/\varepsilon_0$, which in vacuum ($P=0$) reads $E=\varepsilon_0^{-1}D$. Any proposed law $E=\eta D$ with a constant $\eta>0$ of dimension $\mathrm V\,\mathrm m\,\mathrm C^{-1}$ is dimensionally admissible; dimensional consistency therefore does not identify $\eta$, and it does not determine whether the response is local, linear or instantaneous. In the model of [[post-em-material-closure]] the scalar relation is $D=\varepsilon E$, i.e. $\eta=\varepsilon^{-1}$, and $\varepsilon$ (or $\chi_e=\varepsilon/\varepsilon_0-1$) is fixed by the declared material model, not by units.

**(c) [Frequency-domain symbols are not instantaneous coefficients]** In the memory branch of [[post-em-material-closure]](c) the response is a causal convolution in time; a scalar $\varepsilon(\omega)$ introduced in the harmonic description acts on the Fourier components of the field history in the material rest frame. The framework therefore does not read $\varepsilon(\omega)$ as an instantaneous multiplicative coefficient in the time domain: doing so silently replaces the convolution by an instantaneous law and is a model-identification error of the same kind as (a).

Adopt as a modelling postulate of this framework the following reduced circuit description, to be used only within its declared regime. Let the laboratory region, its chart and units and the compact smooth current class be those of [[def-em-lab-geometry]], [[def-em-si-conventions]] and [[def-em-steady-current-regime]], and let the material response be one of the branches of [[post-em-material-closure]].

(b) [Branch relations and network laws] In the declared regime the inductive branches obey the Faraday branch relation $V(t)=L\dot I(t)$, i.e. each terminal potential is the rate of change of the branch flux linkage $LI$; the capacitive branches obey $V=C^{-1}Q$ (in the scalar case $V_\beta=Q_\beta/C_{\beta\beta}$); the resistive branches obey $V=RI$, the circuit form of the Ohmic relation of [[post-em-material-closure]]; and the network laws are Kirchhoff's current law at each node and loop voltage balance around each independent loop. The circuit-level bookkeeping quantities of the model are the flux linkage $LI$ and the stored energies $\tfrac12I^{\mathsf T}LI$ and $\tfrac12Q^{\mathsf T}C^{-1}Q$.

(d) [Status, units and scope] This is an adopted reduced model, not a deduction from the vacuum Maxwell equations; the matrices $L,C,R$ are model data, no microscopic constitutive law beyond the adopted branch of [[post-em-material-closure]] is asserted, and no radiation, distributed-element, nonlinear, hysteretic, leakage or proximity effect is included. SI units consistent with [[def-em-si-conventions]] are used: $V$ in volts, $I$ in amperes, $Q$ in coulombs, $t$ in seconds, $L$ in henries ($\mathrm H=\mathrm V\,\mathrm s\,\mathrm A^{-1}$), $C$ in farads ($\mathrm F=\mathrm C\,\mathrm V^{-1}$) and $R$ in ohms ($\Omega=\mathrm V\,\mathrm A^{-1}$). Where conductor matter moves, material speeds are subluminal, $|v|<c$, when the relativistic force interpretation is used.

The postulate is not derived from the vacuum Maxwell equations, from [[post-em-material-closure]] or from any measurement. The cited textbook treatments present the branch relations as part of the standard circuit model; the exact matrices, the terminal geometry and the loop choice remain model data. Consequences such as the energy bookkeeping, the RL and LC dynamics and the transformer idealisation on this page are conditional derivations from the adopted relations together with the smooth compact-current realization of the inductive couplings, and they inherit the regime declaration of clause (c).

At time $t$ the ideal oriented contour $C(t)$ comprises only the rail portions $a_0\le s\le x(t)$, that left side, and the sliding bar centerline $(x(t),w,0)$. physical_scope: "Flat affine Minkowski spacetime in every inertial chart, under the adopted scalar-field, dust and perfect-fluid model equations of [[post-sr-matter-models-and-evolution]]. The theorem is a conditional deduction from those adopted equations: it asserts no interaction, force law, cross section, measurement or empirical fact, makes no claim for arbitrary prescribed symmetric tensors, and its conclusions inherit the scope and qualifications of the postulate."

Under the matter premises of [[post-sr-matter-models-and-evolution]]: (a) If $\varphi$ is a smooth scalar field solving the adopted field equation $\Box\varphi=V'(\varphi)$ on $\Omega$, then the Hilbert stress-energy tensor of the scalar-field action ([[lem-sr-scalar-field-hilbert-stress-energy]]) satisfies $\partial_aT^{ab}=0$ on $\Omega$, in every inertial chart. (b) If $ho>0$ and the future unit field $n$ satisfy the adopted dust equations, then $T=ho\,n\otimes n$ satisfies $\partial_aT^{ab}=0$; conversely if $\partial_aT^{ab}=0$ and $ho>0$ then the dust equations hold. (c) If $\varepsilon,P$ and the future unit field $n$ satisfy the adopted fluid equations, then $T=(\varepsilon+P)n\otimes n+P\eta$ satisfies $\partial_aT^{ab}=0$; conversely conservation of that $T$ implies the two fluid equations. (d) For a $C^1$ symmetric tensor field prescribed on $\Omega$ that is not obtained from one of the adopted models together with its field equations, no conservation is asserted; a conservation statement about such a field is an additional explicit premise. (e) The theorem is a conditional deduction from the adopted model equations; it asserts no interaction, force law, cross section, measurement or empirical fact, and its conclusions inherit the scope of the postulate. Under the already stated homogeneous dust reading, the tensor boost computation has the conditional physical interpretation $T'^{00}=\gamma^2ho$. For comoving identical massive particles with fixed rest mass $m$, rest number density $
u$ and $ho=
u mc^2$, a rest rectangular parcel has boosted simultaneous volume $1/\gamma$ times its rest volume (the parallel length contracts and transverse lengths are unchanged), so its particle density is $\gamma
u$; the adopted massive-particle reading gives each particle energy $\gamma mc^2$. Thus the two factors in $\gamma^2ho$ correspond respectively to particle energy and volume/density. This is conditional model interpretation for that homogeneous particle realization, not a derivation of the continuum from microscopic dynamics, a claim about arbitrary tensors, or empirical evidence.

**Given:** The affine Minkowski model with inertial chart $x$ and its index conventions ([[def-sr-affine-minkowski-model]]), the adopted matter model equations and readings of [[post-sr-matter-models-and-evolution]], the particle premises and homogeneous dust reading of [[post-sr-massive-particle-dynamics]], and the force-density/conservation terminology of [[def-sr-stress-energy-tensor-and-force-density]] (conservation of a $C^1$ symmetric field $T$ means $\partial_aT^{ab}=0$, and the force density is chart-independent).

[F1] Scalar divergence identity: for the smooth scalar field and Hilbert tensor of the adopted model, $\partial_aT^{ab}=K(\Box\varphi-V'(\varphi))\partial^b\varphi$; in particular any solution of $\Box\varphi=V'(\varphi)$ has conserved Hilbert tensor. ([[lem-sr-scalar-field-stress-divergence-identity]], [[lem-sr-scalar-field-hilbert-stress-energy]])

[F2] Dust equivalence: for $C^1$ $\rho>0$ and a $C^1$ future unit field $n$, $\partial_a(\rho\,n^an^b)=0$ if and only if $\partial_a(\rho n^a)=0$ and $n^a\partial_an^b=0$. ([[lem-sr-dust-conservation-equivalence]])

[F3] Perfect-fluid identity: for the field $T=(\varepsilon+P)n\otimes n+P\eta$, $\partial_aT^{ab}=n^b(D\varepsilon+(\varepsilon+P)\vartheta)+((\varepsilon+P)a^b+h^{bc}\partial_cP)$, and $\partial_aT^{ab}=0$ if and only if both bracket expressions vanish. ([[lem-sr-perfect-fluid-conservation-equations]])

[F4] Massive-particle reading: a particle of rest mass $m$ and four-velocity $U=m^{-1}P$ has energy $E=\gamma mc^2$ in a frame where its speed parameter is $v$ with $\gamma=(1-v^2/c^2)^{-1/2}$; a rest rectangular parcel's parallel length contracts by the factor $1/\gamma$ while transverse lengths are unchanged. ([[lem-sr-four-momentum-in-inertial-frame]], [[lem-sr-boost-time-length-and-velocity-formulas]], [[post-sr-massive-particle-dynamics]])

[F5] Transformation laws: under an inertial transition the components of a $C^1$ type-$(2,0)$ field transform by the rank-two law $T'^{ab}=\Lambda^a{}_c\Lambda^b{}_dT^{cd}$, and its coordinate divergence transforms as a vector, $\partial'_aT'^{ab}=\Lambda^b{}_c\partial_aT^{ac}$, so conservation is a chart-independent statement. ([[def-sr-stress-energy-tensor-and-force-density]], [[thm-sr-tensor-and-current-transformation]]\,(iii),(iv))

1.4 Clause (d). The definition [[def-sr-stress-energy-tensor-and-force-density]] states explicitly in its clause (d) that it asserts no conservation of any prescribed symmetric field, and the present theorem derives conservation only from the adopted model equations of clauses (a)–(c); accordingly for a $C^1$ symmetric field prescribed on $\Omega$ that is not obtained from one of the adopted models together with its field equations, no conservation is asserted, and any conservation statement about such a field would be an additional explicit premise. [given]

1.5 Clause (e), conditional homogeneous-dust reading. Consider a homogeneous dust realization with comoving identical particles of rest mass $m>0$ and rest number density $
u>0$, so that the adopted reading gives $ho=
u mc^2$, and consider a rest rectangular parcel of rest volume $V_0$. Take the tensor $T=ho\,n\otimes n$ in the rest frame, where $n=e_0$, so that $T^{00}=ho$ and all other components vanish. The passive boost with parameter $ eta$ along the parcel's motion direction has $\Lambda^0{}_0=\gamma$ and is proper orthochronous ([[def-lorentz-boost]]), so the rank-two law of [F5] gives $T'^{00}=\Lambda^0{}_a\Lambda^0{}_bT^{ab}=(\Lambda^0{}_0)^2ho=\gamma^2ho$; thus $T'^{00}=\gamma^2
u mc^2=(\gamma mc^2)(\gamma
u)$. In a frame related to the rest frame by that boost the simultaneous volume of the parcel is $V_0/\gamma$ by the length-contraction part of [F4] (parallel length $1/\gamma$, transverse lengths unchanged), so the particle number density in that frame is $
u'=N/(V_0/\gamma)=\gamma
u$; by the massive-particle reading [F4] each particle carries energy $\gamma mc^2$. Hence the two factors in $\gamma^2ho$ correspond respectively to particle energy and volume/density in the boosted frame. This is a conditional interpretation of the factorization within the homogeneous particle realization; it is not a derivation of the continuum model from microscopic dynamics. [F4, F5, given]

relevant_body_uses.text: Let $(V,\eta)$ be the oriented Lorentz vector space of the affine Minkowski model with orientation and volume form $\varepsilon$ of [[def-oriented-minkowski-volume-form]], and let $F:V\times V\to\mathbb R$ be an alternating bilinear form ([[def-alternating-k-linear-map]], [[def-bilinear-symmetric-skew-and-alternating-forms]]). Define the Hodge dual by $(*F)_{ab}:=\tfrac12\varepsilon_{ab}{}^{cd}F_{cd}$ and set $(\alpha\wedge\beta)_{ab}:=\alpha_a\beta_b-\alpha_b\beta_a$. Use the standard form normalization $F=\tfrac12\sum_{a,b}F_{ab}\theta^a\wedge\theta^b$ in the dual coframe $\theta^a(e_b)=\delta^a_b$ of an oriented orthonormal frame, and define $(F\wedge F)(v_0,v_1,v_2,v_3):=2[F(v_0,v_1)F(v_2,v_3)-F(v_0,v_2)F(v_1,v_3)+F(v_0,v_3)F(v_1,v_2)]$, the alternating four-form exterior square. Let $n\in V$ be future unit, $\eta(n,n)=-1$, and put $e_a:=F_{ab}n^b$, $b_a:=(*F)_{ab}n^b$. (a) $e(n)=b(n)=0$, and $F=n^\flat\wedge e-*(n^\flat\wedge b)$ with $n^\flat:=\eta(n,\cdot)$; also $*(*F)=-F$, so the Hodge dual squares to $-1$ on two-forms. (b) In an oriented orthonormal frame with $n=e_0$: $e_i=F_{i0}$, $b_i=-\tfrac12\epsilon_{ijk}F_{jk}$, $F_{0i}=-e_i$ and $F_{ij}=-\epsilon_{ijk}b_k$; hence the six components of $F$ are exactly the six components of the pair $(e,b)$ and the reconstruction in (a) is equivalent to these component formulae. (c) The quadratic invariants are $\tfrac12F_{ab}F^{ab}=|b|^2-|e|^2$ and $F_{ab}(*F)^{ab}=-4\,(e\cdot b)$, where $|\cdot|$ and $\cdot$ are those of the spatial structure of the frame ([[def-spatial-euclidean-structure-of-an-inertial-frame]]); also $F\wedge F=2(e\cdot b)\varepsilon$. The two scalar expressions $I_1:=\tfrac12F_{ab}F^{ab}$ and $I_2:=F_{ab}(*F)^{ab}$ form a basis of the homogeneous quadratic polynomials in the six components of $F$ invariant under the proper orthochronous Lorentz group; the square-wedge expression is dependent, $F\wedge F=-\tfrac12 I_2\varepsilon$. $I_2$ is an oriented pseudoscalar and changes sign if the chosen orientation is reversed with the metric and $F$ held fixed. (d) (Optional SI identification.) Let $c>0$. If in an inertial frame one identifies $F^{i0}=E_i/c$ and $F^{ij}=-\epsilon_{ijk}B_k$ for spatial vector fields $E,B$, then $e_i=-E_i/c$ and $b_i=B_i$, the invariants of (c) read $\tfrac12F_{ab}F^{ab}=|B|^2-|E|^2/c^2$ and $F_{ab}(*F)^{ab}=4\,(E\cdot B)/c$, and $F\wedge F=-2(E\cdot B)\varepsilon/c$. If $\kappa:=(F\wedge F)(e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3)=(F\wedge F)_{0123}$, then $E\cdot B=-c\kappa/2$. Under the passive boost of [[def-lorentz-boost]] along $e_1$ with parameter $\beta\in(-1,1)$ one has $E'_1=E_1$, $B'_1=B_1$, $E'_\perp=\gamma(E+v\times B)_\perp$ and $B'_\perp=\gamma(B-v\times E/c^2)_\perp$ where the cross product is the right-handed product ([[def-cross-product-in-r3]]), with $\gamma=(1-\beta^2)^{-1/2}$ and $v=\beta c$ along $e_1$. (e) The theorem is algebra on the oriented Lorentz vector space with the stated index and duality conventions; clause (d) is an explicitly optional identification of the components of $F$ with fields the electromagnetic framework names $E,B$, and the theorem asserts no field equation, no dynamics, no measurement and no transformation beyond the stated component law. No choice principle is used.

**Given:** The oriented Lorentz vector space $(V,\eta)$ of the affine Minkowski model with its fixed orientation and oriented volume form $\varepsilon$, normalized by $\varepsilon(e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3)=+1$ in every positively oriented orthonormal frame ([[def-oriented-minkowski-volume-form]], [[def-sr-affine-minkowski-model]], [[def-lorentz-form-and-inertia]], [[lem-lorentz-form-has-orthonormal-basis]]); the raised volume form is $\varepsilon^{abcd}=\eta^{aa'}\eta^{bb'}\eta^{cc'}\eta^{dd'}\varepsilon_{a'b'c'd'}$, so $\varepsilon^{0123}=\eta^{00}\eta^{11}\eta^{22}\eta^{33}\varepsilon_{0123}=-1$. An alternating bilinear form $F$ with components $F_{ab}=-F_{ba}$ ([[def-alternating-k-linear-map]], [[def-bilinear-symmetric-skew-and-alternating-forms]]); a future unit $n\in V$ with $\eta(n,n)=-1$ ([[def-causal-classification-of-lorentz-vectors]], [[def-time-orientation-and-future-causal-sets]]); and the conventions $(*F)_{ab}:=\tfrac12\varepsilon_{ab}{}^{cd}F_{cd}$, $(\alpha\wedge\beta)_{ab}:=\alpha_a\beta_b-\alpha_b\beta_a$, the dual coframe $\theta^a(e_b)=\delta^a_b$ ([[def-algebraic-dual-and-linear-functional]]), and $(F\wedge F)(v_0,\dots,v_3):=2[F(v_0,v_1)F(v_2,v_3)-F(v_0,v_2)F(v_1,v_3)+F(v_0,v_3)F(v_1,v_2)]$. The spatial inner product of the frame is the restriction of $-\eta$ to $n^\perp$ ([[def-spatial-euclidean-structure-of-an-inertial-frame]], [[def-euclidean-inner-product]]), and $e_a:=F_{ab}n^b$, $b_a:=(*F)_{ab}n^b$.

[F1] Observer rest space: for future unit $n$ the subspace $n^\perp=\{v:\eta(n,v)=0\}$ is three-dimensional and $\eta$ restricts to a positive definite form on it; the map $h(v)=v+\eta(n,v)n$ has image $n^\perp$ and satisfies $h^a{}_bn^b=0=n_ah^a{}_b$. ([[thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition]]\,(c))

[F3] Tensor transformation and invariance of the volume form: for a proper orthochronous Lorentz map $L$ the components of a $(0,2)$ form satisfy $F'_{ab}=L_a{}^cL_b{}^dF_{cd}$, the alternating covariant laws hold on each slot, and $\varepsilon'_{abcd}=\varepsilon_{abcd}$ (the oriented volume form is invariant); the boosts $B(\beta)$ are proper orthochronous with $B(\beta)^{-1}=B(-\beta)$ and every spatial rotation extension $\operatorname{diag}(1,R)$ is a proper orthochronous Lorentz map. ([[thm-sr-tensor-and-current-transformation]]\,(iii),(v), [[lem-boost-is-proper-orthochronous-with-inverse]], [[lem-boost-rotation-factorization]]\,(iii))

[F4] Passive boost: for $\beta\in(-1,1)$ and $\gamma=(1-\beta^2)^{-1/2}$ the boost along the spatial axis $e_1$ has the matrix $\Lambda^0{}_0=\Lambda^1{}_1=\gamma$, $\Lambda^0{}_1=\Lambda^1{}_0=-\gamma\beta$, and identity on the other two spatial directions; it is proper orthochronous with $B(\beta)^{-1}=B(-\beta)$. Then:

Let $v\in S$, $T,R>0$, and let $(\Phi_{v,C})_{C>|v|}$, $G_v$ and $D_{T,R}$ be as in [[def-sr-galilean-limiting-charts]]. For $C>|v|$ write $\gamma_C:=(1-|v|^2/C^2)^{-1/2}$ and $z:=|v|^2/C^2$, and for $(t,x)\in\mathbb R\times S$ write $\Phi_{v,C}(t,x)=(t',x')$.

**Given:** A vector $v\in S$, reals $T,R>0$, the family $(\Phi_{v,C})_{C>|v|}$, the Galilean map $G_v(t,x)=(t,x-tv)$, the region $D_{T,R}=\{(t,x):|t|\le T,\ |x|\le R\}$, and for $C>|v|$ the numbers $\gamma_C=(1-|v|^2/C^2)^{-1/2}$ and $z=|v|^2/C^2$ ([[def-sr-galilean-limiting-charts]]).

[L1] The definitions of $\Phi_{v,C}$, $G_v$, $D_{T,R}$ and $\gamma_C$ are those of [[def-sr-galilean-limiting-charts]]: for $v\ne0$, $\Phi_{v,C}(t,x)=\bigl(\gamma_C(t-\delta(v,x)/C^2),\ x+((\gamma_C-1)/|v|^2)\delta(v,x)v-\gamma_Ctv\bigr)$, and $\Phi_{0,C}=\mathrm{id}$.

[L2] Uniform Taylor remainder: for $z_0\in(0,1)$, $K_0=\tfrac38(1-z_0)^{-5/2}$ and $0\le z\le z_0$, one has $(1-z)^{-1/2}=1+\tfrac z2+R(z)$ with $|R(z)|\le K_0z^2$, hence $(\gamma-1)\le(\tfrac12+K_0z_0)z$ for $\gamma=(1-z)^{-1/2}$ ([[lem-sr-uniform-low-speed-taylor-remainder]]).

[L3] Cauchy–Schwarz in the frame's orthonormal basis: writing $v=\sum_iv^ie_i$ and $x=\sum_ix^ie_i$ in the $\delta$-orthonormal basis of [[def-spatial-euclidean-structure-of-an-inertial-frame]], one has $\delta(v,x)=\sum_iv^ix^i$, $|v|^2=\sum_i(v^i)^2$, $|x|^2=\sum_i(x^i)^2$ and $|\delta(v,x)|\le|v|\,|x|$ ([[thm-cauchy-schwarz-finite]]).
[L6] The norm $|w|=\sqrt{\delta(w,w)}$ of [[def-spatial-euclidean-structure-of-an-inertial-frame]] is the nonnegative square root of [[thm-of-square-roots]], so $|w|^2=\delta(w,w)$ and $|w|\ge0$.

The statement and proof concern the auxiliary coordinate family $\Phi_{v,C}$ of [[def-sr-galilean-limiting-charts]] alone: $C$ is varied with $v,T,R$ fixed, the model's adopted scale $c$ is unchanged, and no trajectory, force, interaction or physical limiting process is defined. The constants $A_0,\Gamma_0,K_0$ depend on the chosen $z_0$ (equivalently on the admissible ratio $|v|/C$), so the rate is uniform only on the declared bounded region and speed window; clause (d) exhibits the failure outside it. The quantitative threshold of clause (c) is sharp enough for the worked evaluation of [[ex-sr-uniform-galilean-chart-bound-worked]].
Let $\theta$ be an affine phase function with wave covector $k$ ([[def-sr-affine-phase-and-wave-covector]]). Then:

**(b)** if $x:I\to A$ is a future timelike worldline ([[def-sr-regular-causal-curve-and-worldline]]) with proper-time function $\tau$ ([[def-sr-proper-time]]) and four-velocity $U=\mathrm dx/\mathrm d\tau$ ([[def-sr-four-velocity-and-four-acceleration]]), then $\mathrm d(\theta\circ x)/\mathrm d\tau=k(U)$ along the worldline, the derivative being taken in the proper-time parametrization, whose inverse exists by [[lem-sr-proper-time-parametrization]];

**(d)** if $k$ is a future null wave covector and $x$ is the straight worldline of an inertial observer, so that $U=cn$ for a future unit timelike vector $n$ with $\eta(n,n)=-1$, then $k(U)=ck(n)$ and $-k(U)=-ck(n)>0$; conversely every future timelike worldline has $\eta(U,U)=-c^2$ ([[thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition]]).

[L1] $\theta(p)-\theta(q)=k(p-q)$ for all $p,q\in A$, and for every $C^1$ curve $\gamma:I\to A$ one has $(\theta\circ\gamma)'(s)=k(\gamma'(s))$ for all $s\in I$ ([[def-sr-affine-phase-and-wave-covector]], clauses (a) and (b)).

[L2] A future timelike worldline $x:I\to A$ is a $C^1$ curve whose tangent $x'(s)$ is future timelike for every $s$, and the parametrization is part of the curve ([[def-sr-regular-causal-curve-and-worldline]]).

[L3] The proper-time function $\tau$ of a future timelike worldline is $C^1$ and strictly increasing with $\tau'(s)=c^{-1}\sqrt{-\eta(x'(s),x'(s))}>0$; its inverse $\rho:J\to I$ is $C^1$ with $\rho'(\tau(s))=1/\tau'(s)$, and $y:=x\circ\rho$ is a $C^1$ future timelike worldline with $y'(\tau(s))=x'(s)/\tau'(s)$ ([[def-sr-proper-time]], [[lem-sr-proper-time-parametrization]]).

[L4] The four-velocity is $U(s)=x'(s)/\tau'(s)=cx'(s)/\sqrt{-\eta(x'(s),x'(s))}$, it is future timelike, and $\eta(U(s),U(s))=-c^2$ ([[def-sr-four-velocity-and-four-acceleration]], [[thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition]], clause (a)).

[L5] A future null wave covector has $k^\sharp$ nonzero future causal, and for a future timelike vector $n$ and a nonzero future causal vector $v$ one has $\eta(n,v)<0$; moreover $k(w)=\eta(k^\sharp,w)$ for every $w$ ([[def-sr-affine-phase-and-wave-covector]], [[lem-sr-future-causal-pairing-negative]], clause (a)).

Adopt as physical assumptions of this framework, extending [[post-sr-ideal-clocks-and-light]] (ideal vacuum light rays are exactly the future null straight lines, with coordinate speed $c$ in every inertial chart) and [[post-sr-inertial-covariance]] (the affine Minkowski model, with the model's equations covariant under proper orthochronous affine Lorentz maps):

**(i) Ideal plane wave.** An ideal monochromatic light wave in vacuum is modeled, in any inertial chart, by a dimensionless affine phase $\theta$ with future null wave covector $k$ ([[def-sr-affine-phase-and-wave-covector]], [[lem-sr-null-covector-frame-data]]): the level sets of $\theta$ are the wave fronts, every line $p+\mathbb Rk^\sharp$ has constant phase, and the rays of this ideal wave are the future null straight lines $p+\mathbb R_{\ge0}k^\sharp$, consistently with the general ideal-light clause that the ideal vacuum light rays are exactly the future null straight lines. The model is one ideal plane wave: constant wave covector, no medium, no dispersion, no absorption, no modulation or envelope, no boundary or source model, no intensity or polarization model.

**(ii) Frequency reading.** An ideal observer of the model with four-velocity $U_o=cn$ ($n$ future unit timelike) that receives this wave reads the angular frequency $\omega_n:=-ck(n)=-k(U_o)$ and the linear frequency $\omega_n/(2\pi)$ of [[def-sr-null-wave-covector-and-observer-frequency]], that is, minus the rate of change of the phase with respect to the observer's own proper time with the sign convention that this number is positive ([[lem-sr-phase-rate-along-worldline]], [[lem-sr-future-causal-pairing-negative]]). The reading is attached to the observer's worldline at the event of reception.

**(iv) Scope and exclusions.** These are adopted idealizations, not deductions from experiment and not claims about nature. No quantum photon model and no identification of energy with $\hbar\omega$ is made (excluded by the conventions of [[def-sr-si-units-and-coordinate-conventions]]); no claim is made that real light, real clocks, real receivers or real sources are exactly described; dispersive, absorbing, nonlinear or modulated media, finite line width, intensity, polarization, source and detector physics, gravitation, quantum effects and accelerated-observer reception are outside the model. Empirical tests of the model belong to the framework's experimental work and are not asserted here.

Remark on the conventions of [[def-sr-si-units-and-coordinate-conventions]] and [[def-sr-null-wave-covector-and-observer-frequency]], for use with [[pthm-sr-null-wave-doppler-and-aberration]]. The frame data and wave data of a future null wave covector are related as in [[lem-sr-null-covector-frame-data]], and the symbols below have the meanings fixed there and in [[def-sr-affine-phase-and-wave-covector]].

**(b) Two coordinate forms.** In the adopted coordinates $\theta=-\omega t+\kappa\cdot x_{\mathrm{vec}}+\mathrm{const}$ and $k_a=(-\omega/c,(\omega/c)s_1,(\omega/c)s_2,(\omega/c)s_3)$; in a chart whose time coordinate is $t$ in seconds directly, so that the metric component $g_{tt}=-c^2$ carries $\mathrm m^2\mathrm s^{-2}$ and the time-space components carry $\mathrm m\,\mathrm s^{-1}$, the same phase is $\theta=-\omega t+\kappa\cdot x_{\mathrm{vec}}+\mathrm{const}$ with the same $\omega$ and $\kappa$, and the component tuple $(-\omega,(\omega/c)s)$ carries mixed units $(\mathrm s^{-1},\mathrm m^{-1})$ because it is read in the coordinate basis $(\partial_t,\partial_{x^i})$ rather than in the dimensionless frame basis $(e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3)$. Formulas derived in one convention are not reused unchanged in the other; this is the general warning of [[def-sr-si-units-and-coordinate-conventions]] specialized to the wave covector.

**(i) Total tensor.** In every conservation or integration statement of this framework the tensor used is the total stress-energy tensor of the system considered, including every constituent that carries energy-momentum — matter, fields and supporting structures present in the region — assembled by the additivity clause of [[post-sr-matter-models-and-evolution]].

**(ii) Localisation.** Whenever conservation of a slice four-momentum over a coordinate-time interval $[s_1,s_2]$ is asserted in an inertial chart, the model assumes that during that interval the total tensor is $C^1$ and symmetric on a neighbourhood of a closed box $[s_1,s_2]\times\bar K$ ([[def-sr-stress-energy-tensor-and-force-density]], [[def-sr-affine-minkowski-model]]), that its components satisfy the zero side-flux condition $T^{ib}=0$ on the spatial faces of the box for $i=1,2,3$, and that the slice integrals converge; equivalently, the system is isolated inside the chosen region for the chosen interval.

**(iii) Failure of isolation.** If the side flux does not vanish, only the exact finite-flux balance of [[thm-sr-stress-balance-and-finite-flux]] is asserted; no conservation of a slice integral is inferred and no limiting procedure at spatial infinity is adopted.

**(iv) Unmodelled matter.** For a matter system not governed by one of the models of [[post-sr-matter-models-and-evolution]], conservation of its stress-energy tensor is not inferred; if used it must be adopted or derived separately.

The force vocabulary of this framework has two distinct mathematical carriers. On a massive particle worldline the four-force is $F=\dot P=dP/d\tau$ ([[def-sr-proper-time-derivative-and-four-force]]), and its identities are conditional on the adopted particle dynamics [[post-sr-massive-particle-dynamics]]. In the continuum the force carrier is the four-force density $f^b=\partial_aT^{ab}$ of a symmetric type-$(2,0)$ field ([[def-sr-stress-energy-tensor-and-force-density]]). Neither object is a force law: the definition of $\dot P$ asserts no equation of motion, and the definition of $f$ asserts no conservation and no interaction.

In case (i), $\psi(p,t)=g_D(p,t)$ on $\partial\Omega\times I$, and its restriction to $\Omega\times I$ is unique with those Dirichlet values. In case (ii), $\varepsilon_0\partial_\nu\psi(p,t)=\kappa(p,t)$ there, and imposing $\int_{\Omega_j}\psi(\cdot,t)\,dx=0$ for every component and every $t$ gives a unique generator on $\Omega\times I$; without that normalization it is unique modulo smooth time-dependent spatial constants on each component. The transformed pair $T_\psi(\varphi,A)$ is in Coulomb gauge and has the same physical field pair ([[pthm-em-gauge-invariance]]). Any two Coulomb-gauge generators differ by a function spatially harmonic at every $t$; equal Dirichlet data eliminate that residual freedom, whereas equal Neumann data leave only the componentwise constants just described. Zero Dirichlet data are the corresponding special case. Auxiliary ambient continuations away from the physical region need not be unique.

coordinate_mentions.text: 1.7 The two hemispheres as $C^2$ patches and their induced boundaries. The rectangles $D_N=[0,\pi/2]\times[0,2\pi]$ and $D_S=[\pi/2,\pi]\times[0,2\pi]$ are Type I and Type II regions, hence elementary Green regions with their positive boundary chains in the sense of [F8], and the restrictions of $\Phi$ to them are $C^2$ on an open neighbourhood with nonvanishing cross product and injective interior, so they are $C^2$ patches over finite elementary Green regions with induced boundary chains as in [F8]. For a rectangle $[a,b]\times[c,d]$ the positive boundary chain runs along the lower graph from left to right, up the right side, back along the upper graph and down the left side [F8]. Under $\Phi$ and using the periods of sine and cosine from [F5], the lower and upper graphs have the same image, namely the meridian $\phi\mapsto(\sin\phi,0,\cos\phi)$ on $[a,b]$, traversed in opposite directions; the left side of $D_N$ lies at $\phi=0$, where $\Phi(0,\theta)=(0,0,1)$ is constant, and the right side of $D_S$ lies at $\phi=\pi$, where $\Phi(\pi,\theta)=(0,0,-1)$ is constant; the right side of $D_N$ and the left side of $D_S$ both equal the equator $\theta\mapsto(\cos\theta,\sin\theta,0)$, traversed in the positive and in the reverse direction respectively. Thus the north induced boundary chain consists of a meridian arc, the equator, the reversed meridian arc and a degenerate polar arc, and the south induced boundary chain consists of a meridian arc, a degenerate polar arc, the reversed meridian arc and the reversed equator. [given, F5, F8]
